Definition 4.7 & Theorem 4.8: Generative Context \(U_{\mathsf{G}}\) & Slice-Site Equivalence
  • Def. 4.7 (Context Object \(U_{\mathsf{G}}\)): A Generative blueprint \(\mathsf{G}\) specifies an admissible context \(U_{\mathsf{G}} \in \mathbf{Ctx}_{\mathrm{adm}}^{\mathrm{sk}}\) whose 4-store carrier space is \(P^{U_{\mathsf{G}}} \cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^4 \mathbb{R}^3_i \cong \mathbb{R}^{12}\), maintaining strict 3-way space separation between base manifold \(M_{U_{\mathsf{G}}}\), linear carrier \(P^{U_{\mathsf{G}}}\), and gauge Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{g}\).
  • Thm. 4.8 (Slice-Site Topos Equivalence for \(T0\)): Let \((\mathbf{Ctx}_{/U_{\mathsf{G}}}, J_{/U_{\mathsf{G}}})\) be the localized slice site over \(U_{\mathsf{G}}\). Because \(J_{\mathrm{syn}}\) is subcanonical, there is a canonical equivalence of Grothendieck toposes realizing the Syntrixtotalität \(T0\): \[T0 \;\simeq\; \mathbf{Sh}\!\left(\mathbf{Ctx}_{/U_{\mathsf{G}}}, \, J_{/U_{\mathsf{G}}}\right) \;\simeq\; \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{syn}} \big/ \mathbf{y}(U_{\mathsf{G}}).\]
Proof of Theorem 4.8 & Scholium: Relative Universes of Potential

Proof: By general topos theory (Mac Lane & Moerdijk 1992, III.7; Johnstone 2002, C2.2), for any object \(U_{\mathsf{G}}\) in a site \((\mathcal{C}, J)\), the slice category \(\mathbf{Sh}(\mathcal{C}, J)/\mathbf{a}(\mathbf{y}(U_{\mathsf{G}}))\) is equivalent to \(\mathbf{Sh}(\mathcal{C}_{/U_{\mathsf{G}}}, J_{/U_{\mathsf{G}}})\). Since \(J_{\mathrm{syn}}\) is subcanonical (Prop. 1.24), \(\mathbf{a}(\mathbf{y}(U_{\mathsf{G}})) = \mathbf{y}(U_{\mathsf{G}})\). \(\blacksquare\)
Scholium (Zalamea 2012): Slicing \(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{syn}}\) over \(\mathbf{y}(U_{\mathsf{G}})\) relativizes the internal logic without collapsing the ambient universe: every sheaf morphism \(F \to \mathbf{y}(U_{\mathsf{G}})\) is a family of local realizations indexed by sub-contexts \(V \to U_{\mathsf{G}}\).

Definition 4.9: Globally Complete Tangent Enyphane Flows on Corners
On a parameter manifold with corners \(\mathcal{M} = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\), an Admissible Enyphane Vector Field \(X \in \mathfrak{X}_{\partial}(\mathcal{M})\) satisfies:

Sub-Linear Growth (Grönwall Completeness): \(\|X(x)\| \le C_1 + C_2\|x\|\), guaranteeing by Picard–Lindelöf and Grönwall’s Inequality a globally complete 1-parameter diffeomorphism group \(\{\varphi_t^X\}_{t \in \mathbb{R}} \subset \operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{M})\) with sheaf pullback flow \(\Phi_t^X = (\varphi_t^X)^*\) and exact inverse \(\Phi_{-t}^X = \Phi_t^{-X}\).

§4.2.4 Yang–Mills Action Functional & Graded BRST Cohomology

DEFINITION 4.10: YANG–MILLS EQUATION D_A* F_A = 0 PROPOSITION 4.11: GRADED BRST COHOMOLOGY & CLAIM CEILING c_BRST

Definition 4.10: Yang–Mills Action & Pseudo-Riemannian Adjoint \(D_A^*\)

On an \(n\)-dimensional manifold \((M_U, g_U)\) with metric signature index \(s\) (e.g. \(s=0\) Riemannian, \(s=1\) Lorentzian \(R_4\)):
1. Yang–Mills Action Functional:
\[\mathcal{I}(\mathbf{A}) \;\coloneqq\; \frac{1}{2}\int_{M_U} \langle F_A \wedge *F_A \rangle_{\operatorname{ad}P_U} \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\int_{M_U} \|F_A\|_{g_U,\mathfrak{g}}^2 \, d\operatorname{vol}_{g_U}.\]
2. Stationary Critical Point Equation:
Using formal \(L^2\)-adjoint \(D_A^* = (-1)^{n(k-1)+1+s} * D_A *\), \(\delta\mathcal{I}_{\mathbf{A}}(a) = 0 \iff \mathbf{D_A^* F_A = 0}\).

Proposition 4.11: Graded BRST Differential & \(H^0_{\mathrm{BRST}}\) Cohomology

On extended graded configuration algebra \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}} = \bigoplus_{g \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathcal{F}^g\) with ghost numbers \(\operatorname{gh}(\mathbf{A})=0\), \(\operatorname{gh}(c)=+1\), \(\operatorname{gh}(\bar{c})=-1\), \(\operatorname{gh}(b)=0\):
\[s_{\mathrm{BRST}}\mathbf{A} = D_A c, \qquad s_{\mathrm{BRST}}c = -\tfrac{1}{2}[c,c], \qquad s_{\mathrm{BRST}}\bar{c} = b, \qquad s_{\mathrm{BRST}}b = 0.\]
Then \(s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 \equiv 0\) identically, and gauge-invariant observables form the ghost-number-zero cohomology \(H^0_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}})\).

Claim Ceiling (\(c_{\mathrm{BRST}}\)): \(s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 = 0\) is an exact algebraic identity in Stratum \(\mathbf{A}\); physical Hilbert-space unitarity of quantized \({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\) gauge fields remains an open physical hypothesis \([\mathbf{P}]\).

Interactive 4-Tab Yang–Mills & BRST Nilpotency Proof Inspector

\[\mathcal{F}^{-1}\;(\bar{c}) \xlongrightarrow{s_{\mathrm{BRST}}\bar{c} = b} \mathcal{F}^0\;(\mathbf{A}, b) \xlongrightarrow{s_{\mathrm{BRST}}\mathbf{A} = D_A c} \mathcal{F}^1\;(c) \xlongrightarrow{s_{\mathrm{BRST}}c = -\frac{1}{2}[c,c]} \mathcal{F}^2\;([c,c])\] Because \(\deg_\Omega(c)=0\) and \(\operatorname{gh}(c)=1\), \(c\) has odd total degree \(|c|=1\), so the graded commutator \([c,c]\) is symmetric rather than vanishing!

Nilpotency on Ghost Field \(c\) (Graded Jacobi Identity): \[s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 c \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl([s_{\mathrm{BRST}}c, c] - [c, s_{\mathrm{BRST}}c]\bigr) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}[[c,c], c] \;\equiv\; 0\] since for any odd element \(|c|=1\), the graded Jacobi identity gives \(3[[c,c],c] = 0\).

Nilpotency on Connection \(\mathbf{A}\) (Graded Leibniz + Jacobi): \[s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 \mathbf{A} \;=\; d(s_{\mathrm{BRST}}c) + [s_{\mathrm{BRST}}\mathbf{A}, c] - [\mathbf{A}, s_{\mathrm{BRST}}c] \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}d[c,c] + [dc + [\mathbf{A},c], c] + \tfrac{1}{2}[\mathbf{A}, [c,c]] \;\equiv\; 0\]

Cohomological Extraction of Gauge-Invariant States:
Closed states \(\Psi \in \ker(s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathcal{F}^0})\) are gauge-invariant, while exact states \(\operatorname{im}(s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathcal{F}^{-1}})\) are pure gauge artifacts.

§4.3.1 Stratum B1: Relative Interaction Curvature Decomposition Theorem

THEOREM 4.12: INTERACTION CURVATURE 2-FORM Ω_int^𝒟 COROLLARY 4.14: FLAT-COMPONENT REDUCTION & 4-STEP PROOF

Intuition: Enyphanie as the Twist of Misaligned Perspectives

Two locally flat survey maps can fail to agree after parallel transport around a closed loop. Their mismatch is measured by a Lie commutator \([a_1, a_2]\): interaction curvature \(\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}}\) records the exact geometric friction generated when independent viewpoints fail to commute.

Scholium: The Non-Abelian Origin of Interaction Energy

For a non-Abelian connection, \(F_A = dA + \frac{1}{2}[A, A]\). When \(N\) constituent potentials \(a_k\) couple on a common bundle, the cross-commutators \([a_i, a_j]\) (\(i < j\)) survive subtraction of the individual curvatures \(\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)}\), providing the exact mathematical identity of Heim’s Enyphanie.

Theorem 4.12: Relative Interaction Curvature Decomposition Theorem

Let \(\mathbf{A} = A_0 + \sum_{k=1}^N a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}\) be a coupled connection on \(\pi \colon P_U \to M_U\) over reference connection \(A_0\), with constituent curvatures \(\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \coloneqq \frac{1}{N}F_{A_0} + D_{A_0}a_k + \frac{1}{2}[a_k, a_k] \in \Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U)\). Then the total curvature 2-form decomposes identically as: \[F_A \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^N \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \;+\; \mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\mathbf{A}; \mathcal{D})\] where the Interaction Curvature 2-Form \(\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}} \in \Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U)\) is: \[\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\mathbf{A}; \mathcal{D}) \;\coloneqq\; \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N} [a_i, a_j] \;+\; D_{A_0}a_{\mathrm{int}} \;+\; \sum_{k=1}^N [a_k, a_{\mathrm{int}}] \;+\; \frac{1}{2}[a_{\mathrm{int}}, a_{\mathrm{int}}].\]

Corollary 4.14: Immediate Flat-Component Reduction

If all constituent curvature contributions vanish (\(\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \equiv 0\) for all \(k=1,\dots,N\)), then \(F_A \not\equiv 0 \iff \mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\mathbf{A}; \mathcal{D}) \not\equiv 0\).

Proof of Theorem 4.12 (4-Step Coordinate-Free Derivation on \(\Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U)\))
  1. Step 1 (Affine Lift to \(P_U\)): The difference \(a \coloneqq \mathbf{A} - A_0\) is a horizontal, \(G\)-equivariant 1-form \(\widetilde{a} \in \Omega^1_{\mathrm{hor,eq}}(P_U, \mathfrak{g}) \cong \Omega^1(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U)\). Expanding Cartan’s structure equation \(\widetilde{F}_{\mathbf{A}} = d\mathbf{A} + \frac{1}{2}[\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{A}]\) yields the global coordinate-free identity in \(\Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U)\): \[F_A \;=\; F_{A_0} + D_{A_0}a + \frac{1}{2}[a, a].\]
  2. Step 2 (Linearity of \(D_{A_0}\)): Substituting \(a = \sum_{k=1}^N a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}\) into \(D_{A_0}a\) gives \(D_{A_0}a = \sum_{k=1}^N D_{A_0}a_k + D_{A_0}a_{\mathrm{int}}\).
  3. Step 3 (Bilinear Bracket Expansion): Expanding the symmetric graded Lie bracket \(\frac{1}{2}[a,a]\) on 1-forms (\([a_i, a_j] = [a_j, a_i]\)) across the \(N+1\) summands gives: \[\frac{1}{2}[a,a] \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^N [a_k, a_k] + \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N}[a_i, a_j] + \sum_{k=1}^N [a_k, a_{\mathrm{int}}] + \frac{1}{2}[a_{\mathrm{int}}, a_{\mathrm{int}}].\]
  4. Step 4 (Background Partition): Writing \(F_{A_0} = \sum_{k=1}^N \frac{1}{N}F_{A_0}\) and grouping diagonal terms into \(\sum_{k=1}^N \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)}\) leaves \(\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\mathbf{A}; \mathcal{D})\). \(\blacksquare\)

Remark: Worked Example — Non-Abelian \(\mathfrak{su}(2)\) Interaction Curvature

Consider \(G = \mathrm{SU}(2)\) with Lie algebra basis \([T_a, T_b] = \epsilon_{abc}T_c\). Set \(A_0 = 0\), \(a_{\mathrm{int}} = 0\), and consider two uncoupled gauge potentials along orthogonal coordinates \((x, y)\): \[a_1 = T_1 \, dx, \qquad a_2 = T_2 \, dy.\] Individually, both connections are strictly flat: \(\mathcal{F}_1 = da_1 + \frac{1}{2}[a_1, a_1] = 0\) and \(\mathcal{F}_2 = da_2 + \frac{1}{2}[a_2, a_2] = 0\). Yet when coupled on the same bundle, their total curvature is non-zero: \[F_A \;=\; \mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2] \;=\; [T_1, T_2]\,dx \wedge dy \;=\; \mathbf{T_3\,dx \wedge dy \ne 0}!\]

Definition 4.19: Canonical Quadratic Realization of Enyphaniegrad (\(g_E^{\mathcal{D}}\))

Fixing the canonical Yang–Mills Hamiltonian normalization \(c_E \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}\), the local gauge-invariant Enyphaniegrad Energy Density and integrated interaction energy are: \[g_E^{\mathcal{D}}(x) \;\coloneqq\; \frac{1}{2}\bigl\|\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}}(x)\bigr\|_{g_U, \mathfrak{g}}^2 \;=\; \frac{1}{4}g_U^{ia}g_U^{jb}\bigl\langle \mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int},ij}^{\mathcal{D}}(x), \mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int},ab}^{\mathcal{D}}(x)\bigr\rangle_{\operatorname{ad}P_U} \ge 0, \qquad \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}} \coloneqq \int_{M_U} g_E^{\mathcal{D}}(x)\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_U}.\]

Let polarimeter \(\mathcal{S}_a\) induce \(a_1 = \omega_1(x_1)T_1\,dx^1\) and \(\mathcal{S}_b\) induce \(a_2 = \omega_2(x_2)T_2\,dx^2\) over \(A_0 = 0, a_{\mathrm{int}} = 0\):

Theorem 4.13: Non-Flat 2-Way Fredholm Laplacian Splitting

On a compact oriented Riemannian manifold \((M_U, g_U)\), the strongly elliptic Hodge-type Connection Laplacian \(\Delta_{A_0} \coloneqq D_{A_0}D_{A_0}^* + D_{A_0}^*D_{A_0}\) on \(L^2\Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U)\) induces the \(L^2\)-orthogonal Fredholm splitting: \[L^2\Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad}P_U) \;=\; \operatorname{im}(\Delta_{A_0}) \;\oplus_{L^2}\; \mathcal{H}_{\Delta_{A_0}}^2, \qquad \mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}} \;=\; \Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}} \;+\; \gamma_{\mathrm{harm}}\] where \(\Phi_{\mathrm{int}} = G_{A_0}(\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}})\) is the Green potential and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}} \in \ker(\Delta_{A_0})\), yielding exact Energy Orthogonality: \(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathcal{D}} = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\|\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}}\|_{L^2}^2 + \|\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2\bigr)\).

Claim Ceiling (\(c_{\mathrm{LAPLACE}}\)): 2-way splitting \(\operatorname{im}(\Delta_{A_0}) \oplus_{L^2} \ker(\Delta_{A_0})\) holds for all \(A_0\); 3-way Hodge splitting \(\operatorname{im}(D_{A_0}) \oplus \operatorname{im}(D_{A_0}^*) \oplus \mathcal{H}_{A_0}^2\) requires \(D_{A_0}^2 = 0\) (e.g. flat \(F_{A_0} = 0\)).

Defs. 4.15–4.16 & Thm. 4.17: Matching Equalizer, \(\Delta_{\mathrm{emerg}}^{\mathcal{I}}\) & Atiyah Algebroid
  • Defs. 4.15–4.16 (Holoform Emergence): For \(\Gamma \in \mathsf{Match}_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbf{P}) \cong \mathbf{P}(U)\), the background-normalized emergence functional is \(\Delta_{\mathrm{emerg}}^{\mathcal{I}}(\Gamma;\mathcal{D}) \coloneqq \mathcal{I}(\mathbf{A}) - \sum_{k=1}^N \mathcal{I}(A_0+a_k) + (N-1)\mathcal{I}(A_0)\). \(\Gamma\) is a Superadditive Holoform iff \(\Delta_{\mathrm{emerg}}^{\mathcal{I}} > 0\).
  • Thm. 4.17 (Atiyah Lie Algebroid \(\operatorname{At}(P_U) = TP_U/G\)): Fits into \(0 \to \operatorname{ad}P_U \xrightarrow{\iota} \operatorname{At}(P_U) \xrightarrow{a=d\pi_U} TM_U \to 0\). A connection \(\mathbf{A}\) is a splitting \(\sigma_{\mathbf{A}} \colon TM_U \to \operatorname{At}(P_U)\), and \(F_A\) is the exact Lie-bracket obstruction: \[\iota\!\left(F_A(X, Y)\right) \;=\; \bigl[\sigma_{\mathbf{A}}(X), \sigma_{\mathbf{A}}(Y)\bigr]_{\operatorname{At}(P_U)} - \sigma_{\mathbf{A}}\!\left([X, Y]_{TM_U}\right).\]
Theorem 4.18 & Proof: Chern–Weil Bogomolny Stability Bound for Holoformen

On a compact oriented Riemannian 4-manifold \((M_4, g_4)\) with instanton charge \(Q_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathbf{A}) \coloneqq \frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{M_4}\langle F_A \wedge F_A \rangle_{\mathfrak{g}} \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}\), decomposing \(F_A = F_A^+ + F_A^-\) (\(*F_A^\pm = \pm F_A^\pm\)) gives: \[0 \le \frac{1}{4}\int_{M_4}\|F_A \mp *F_A\|^2\,d\operatorname{vol} = \mathcal{I}(\mathbf{A}) \mp 4\pi^2 Q_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathbf{A}) \implies \mathbf{\mathcal{I}(\mathbf{A}) \ge 4\pi^2 |Q_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathbf{A})|}\] with saturation iff \(*F_A = \pm F_A\). By Chern–Weil homotopy invariance, a Holoform with \(|Q_{\mathrm{top}}| \ge 1\) cannot decay continuously to \(Q_{\mathrm{top}} = 0\)! \(\blacksquare\)

For a Syntrixfunktor of valency \(r\) acting on \(N \ge r\) distinct Gebilde, Heim’s output counts are: \[Z_{\mathrm{sym}} = \binom{N}{r}, \qquad Z_{k\text{-asym}} = k!\binom{N}{r}\binom{r}{k} \;\;(0 \le k \le r), \qquad Z_{\mathrm{asym}} = r!\binom{N}{r} = \frac{N!}{(N-r)!}.\] (For \(N < r\), the functor can operate only homometrally.)

Syndromatische Tektonik (Horizontal / Syndrome Tectonics): The horizontal, sequential organization of syndrome layers generated within a given grade by the active synkolators \({}^k\mathfrak{f}\). 3. §5.1.4–5.1.5: Syntrokline Metroplexbrücken & Metroplexdiabatik

STRATUM D: SYNTROKLINE BRÜCKEN (SM EQS. 25, 25a), EN-KOMBINATION (SM-26) & RÜCKKOPPELUNG

Syntrokline Metroplexbrücken (SM Eqs. 25, 25a, pp. 94–98): Totalities \(T_n\) act as Etagen (floors); bridges \({}^{n+N}\alpha\) act as Aufzüge (elevators) lifting lower-grade structures across \(N\) intervening grades: \[ \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n+N}{\tilde{\alpha}} \;\equiv\; \underset{n}{\overset{n+N}{\mathrm{S}}}\, \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \Big[ \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n-1}{\widetilde{\Phi}}_{j(n)\gamma}\big) \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n-1}{\widetilde{\mathrm{f}}}_{j(n)\gamma}, \underline{\mathrm{m}}_{j(n)\gamma}\big) \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\widetilde{\mathrm{f}}}_\gamma, \underline{\mathrm{r}}_\gamma\big) \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n+1}{\widetilde{\mathrm{f}}}, \mathrm{p}\big) \Big]_{\gamma=1}^{k_{(n)}} \tag{SM-25a} \] Endogene Kombinationen (SM Eq. 26, p. 102): \[ \overset{\scriptscriptstyle\sim}{\mathbf{M}}{}^n \;\equiv\; \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \,\mathrm{EN}\, \overset{\scriptscriptstyle p+q}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{b}} \qquad (p + q \le n \;\land\; q > 0) \tag{SM-26} \]

Remark (Conceptual Preamble: Why Higher Scale Hierarchies Require an \((\infty,1)\)-Topos): Following Marquis (2009), Zalamea (2012), and Lurie (2009), when a system of Syntrices is bundled into a higher-grade Metroplex, corporate transformations become 1-morphisms, transformations between those become 2-morphisms, and so on ad infinitum. In strict 1-category theory, forcing multi-scale identifications to hold as rigid point-set equalities causes the hierarchy to collapse into inconsistency. In an \((\infty,1)\)-topos, composition is governed by coherent higher homotopies rather than brittle strict equality.

§5.2.1: Ambient \((\infty, 1)\)-Topos \(\Xsyn\) & Universe Stratification

STRATUM A: META-THEORETIC JUSTIFICATION, DEF. 5.1 & CUMULATIVE UNIVERSES (FIG. 5.2)

Scholium (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Ambient \((\infty,1)\)-Topos & Dendroidal Segal Objects): Why formulate the Metroplex hierarchy inside a single ambient \((\infty, 1)\)-topos \(\Xsyn = \mathbf{Sh}_\infty(\Ctx, \Jsyn)\) rather than iterating sites \(\mathbf{Site}_{n+1} = \mathbf{Sh}(\mathbf{Site}_n)\)? 1. Universe Safety (\(\mathcal{U}_0 \in \mathcal{U}_1 \in \mathcal{U}_2\)): Iterated site-building explodes set-theoretic universes at every step. Housing all grades inside a single \(\mathcal{U}_0\)-presentable \((\infty,1)\)-topos ensures every Metroplex \(\mathbf{M}^n\) remains \(\mathcal{U}_0\)-small inside \(\Xsyn\). 2. Dendroidal Complete Segal Objects (\(\dCSeg(\Xsyn)\)): Because synkolators \(f \in \Osyn(m)\) have multi-ary valence \(m \ge 1\), grade-1 Hypersyntrices are modeled over the Moerdijk–Weiss tree category \(\mathbf{\Omega}\), avoiding strict associativity pitfalls via Rezk’s completeness condition. 3. Adjoint Syntroclinic Bridges: Change-of-operad adjunctions \((\phi_{n, n+N})_! \dashv (\phi_{n, n+N})^*\) replace ad-hoc cross-scale mappings.

Definition 5.1: Ambient \((\infty, 1)\)-Topos \(\Xsyn\) & Postnikov Tower Fix Grothendieck universes \(\mathcal{U}_0 \in \mathcal{U}_1 \in \mathcal{U}_2\) and \(\mathcal{S} \coloneqq \mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{U}_0}\). The Ambient Syntrometric \((\infty, 1)\)-Topos is the left-exact topological localization: \[ \Xsyn \;\coloneqq\; \mathbf{Sh}_\infty\big(\Ctx, \Jsyn\big) \;\coloneqq\; L_{\Jsyn}\!\Big(\operatorname{Fun}\big((\Ctx)^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathcal{S}\big)\Big) \] 1. 0-Truncated Recovery: \(\tau_{\le 0}\Xsyn \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(\Ctx, \Jsyn) = \Esyn\) recovers the 1-topos of Chapter 1. 2. Higher Homotopy Truncation: \(\tau_{\le m} \colon \Xsyn \to \Xsyn^{\le m}\) is left adjoint to the inclusion \(\iota_m \colon \Xsyn^{\le m} \hookrightarrow \Xsyn\).

Size Discipline & Cumulative Universe Stratification (Fig. 5.2): * \(\mathcal{U}_0\) (Internal): Small site \(\Ctx\), objects \(X \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Xsyn)\), internal Metroplexe \(\mathbf{M}^n \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Met_n(\Xsyn))\). * \(\mathcal{U}_1\) (Ambient): Space \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{U}_0}\), topos \(\Xsyn\), categories \(\Met_n(\Xsyn)\) and \(\Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn)\) (\(\mathcal{U}_0\)-presentable, locally \(\mathcal{U}_0\)-small). * \(\mathcal{U}_2\) (Meta-Slice): External functor categories \(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}, \Met_n(\Xsyn))\), external slice totalities \(T_n^{\mathrm{ext}}\), or enlarged \(\Xsyn^{(k)} \coloneqq \mathbf{Sh}_\infty(\Ctx, \Jsyn; \mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{U}_k})\).

§5.2.2–5.2.3: Dendroidal Complete Segal Spaces & Grafting Proof

STRATUM A/B: DENDROIDAL SEGAL SPACES (DEF. 5.2), GRAFTING PROOF (PROP. 5.3) & OPERAD AXIOM (ASSUMP. 5.4)

Definition 5.2: Dendroidal Complete Segal Objects \(\dCSeg(\Xsyn)\) Let \(\mathbf{\Omega}\) be the Moerdijk–Weiss dendroidal category of finite rooted trees (\(i \colon \mathbf{\Delta} \hookrightarrow \mathbf{\Omega}\) embedding linear trees \([k]\)). A dendroidal object \(X \colon \mathbf{\Omega}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \Xsyn\) is a Dendroidal Complete Segal Space (\(X \in \dCSeg(\Xsyn)\)) if: 1. Dendroidal Segal Condition: For every tree \(T \in \mathbf{\Omega}\) with vertices \(V(T)\) and \(n(v)\)-corollas \(C_{n(v)} \hookrightarrow T\) glued along inner edges \(E_{\mathrm{int}}(T)\): \[ X(T) \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \lim_{v \in V(T)}^{\Xsyn} X(C_{n(v)}) \;\simeq\; X(C_{n(v_1)}) \mathop{\times}\limits^{\mathrm{h}}_{X(\eta_{e_1})} \cdots \mathop{\times}\limits^{\mathrm{h}}_{X(\eta_{e_k})} X(C_{n(v_{k+1})}) \] 2. Rezk Completeness: \((i^*X)_0 \xrightarrow{\sim} (i^*X)_{\mathrm{hoequiv}} \subset (i^*X)_1\).

Proposition 5.3 & Proof (Explicit Dendroidal Segal Grafting for Binary Hypersyntrices): Let \(T = C_2^{(v)} \circ_e C_2^{(u)} \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathbf{\Omega})\) graft two binary 2-corollas along inner edge \(\eta_e\). 1. Grafting Pullback: The dendroidal spine is the pushout \(\operatorname{Sc}[T] = C_2^{(v)} \amalg_{\eta_e} C_2^{(u)}\) in \(\mathbf{\Omega}\), mapping to the homotopy pullback \(X(T) \xrightarrow{\sim} X(C_2^{(v)}) \times_{X(\eta_e)}^{\mathrm{h}} X(C_2^{(u)})\) in \(\Xsyn\). 2. Ternary Composite \(\partial_{\eta_e}^* \colon X(T) \to X(C_3)\): Contracting \(\eta_e\) gives the inner face \(\partial_{\eta_e} \colon C_3 \hookrightarrow T\). Inverting the Segal equivalence up to homotopy and applying \(\partial_{\eta_e}^*\) composes compatible binary operations \((v, u) \mapsto v \circ_e u \in X(C_3)\). 3. Associativity Homotopy: On a 3-vertex tree \(T_3\) with inner edges \(e_1, e_2\), commuting face maps \(\partial_{e_1}\partial_{e_2} = \partial_{e_2}\partial_{e_1} \colon C_4 \hookrightarrow T_3\) induce \((w \circ_1 v) \circ_1 u \simeq w \circ_1 (v \circ_2 u)\) inside \(X(C_4)\). \(\blacksquare\)

Interactive Dendroidal Corolla Grafting & Segal Spine Explorer (Prop. 5.3)

Context (§5.2.2, Prop. 5.3): Step through the dendroidal Segal condition on the grafted binary tree \(T = C_2^{(v)} \circ_e C_2^{(u)}\), the inner-edge contraction \(\partial_{\eta_e}\) yielding the composite ternary corolla \(C_3\), and the 3-vertex associativity homotopy.

Assumption 5.4: The Metroplex Operadic Realization Axiom (\(\{\On\}_{n \ge 0}\)) There exists an inductive family of internal \((\infty, 1)\)-operads \(\{\On\}_{n \ge 0}\) in \(\Xsyn\) (\(\mathcal{O}_0 \coloneqq N_\Delta(\Osyn)\)) with: 1. Free-Forgetful Monad Adjunction: \(\Free_{\On} \colon \Xsyn \rightleftarrows \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn) \colon U_n\) (\(T_{\On} = U_n \circ \Free_{\On}\)). 2. Change-of-Operad Adjunctions: Operad morphisms \(\phi_{n, n+1} \colon \On \to \mathcal{O}_{n+1}\) induce \((\phi_{n, n+1})_! \colon \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn) \rightleftarrows \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_{n+1}}(\Xsyn) \colon (\phi_{n, n+1})^*\), with \(\phi_{n, n+N} \coloneqq \phi_{n+N-1, n+N} \circ \dots \circ \phi_{n, n+1}\).

§5.3.1: Uniform Metroplex Categories \(\Met_n(\Xsyn)\) & Toy Example

STRATUM B: UNIFORM METROPLEX CATEGORIES (DEFS. 5.5–5.6), TOY EXAMPLE & 3D TRANSCENDENCE TOWER (FIG. 5.1)

Definition 5.5: Uniform Categories of Grade-\(n\) Metroplexe \(\Met_n(\Xsyn)\) For every grade \(n \ge 0\), \(\Met_n(\Xsyn)\) is a full \((\infty, 1)\)-subcategory of \(\Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn)\): 1. Grade \(n = 0\) (Base Syntrices): \(\Met_0(\Xsyn) \coloneqq \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_0}(\Xsyn)\). 2. Grade \(n = 1\) (Hypersyntrices): \(\Met_1(\Xsyn) \simeq \dCSeg(\Xsyn) \hookrightarrow \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_1}(\Xsyn)\) (with linear spine \(i^*\Met_1(\Xsyn) = \CSeg(\Xsyn) \simeq \operatorname{Cat}_\infty(\Xsyn)\)). 3. Grade \(n \ge 2\) (Higher Metroplexe): \(\Met_n(\Xsyn) \subseteq \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn)\) generated by hypermetrophoric colimits of grade-\((n-1)\) diagrams. Equipped with conservative forgetful functors \(U_n^{\Met} \colon \Met_n(\Xsyn) \to \Xsyn\).

Definition 5.6: Hypermetrophors as Simplicial Diagrams \(H_n\) For \(n \ge 1\), a Grade-\(n\) Hypermetrophor is a simplicial diagram \(H_n \colon \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \Met_{n-1}(\Xsyn)\) whose vertices \([0] \mapsto H_{n,0}\) are grade-\((n-1)\) Metroplexe and whose 1-simplices \([1] \mapsto H_{n,1}\) encode corporate pairings (\(\mathbf{Kor}_n\)). Its geometric realization colimit is: \[ \HypMet_n \;\coloneqq\; \colim_{[k] \in \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}} \big( U_{n-1}^{\Met} \circ H_n([k]) \big) \;\in\; \Xsyn, \qquad \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\mathcal{S} \;\coloneqq\; \Free_{\On}(\HypMet_n) \]

Remark (Toy Example: The Hypersyntrix \(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\) as an Internal 2-Object Category): Consider two base Syntrices \(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2 \in \Met_0(\Xsyn)\) coupled by a corporate pairing \(\mathbf{Kor}(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2)\). How do they form a grade-1 Hypersyntrix \(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}} \in \CSeg(\Xsyn)\)? * Object Space (\([0]\)): \(C_0 \coloneqq \mathcal{S}_1 \sqcup \mathcal{S}_2\) (the Hypermetrophor \({}^1\mathbf{w}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}}\)). Every entire lower-level Syntrix becomes a single point (0-simplex) at grade 1! * Morphism Space (\([1]\)): \(C_1 \coloneqq \mathbf{Kor}(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2) \sqcup \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{S}_1} \sqcup \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{S}_2}\) (the Metroplexsynkolator \({}^1\mathfrak{f}\)). * Segal Composition (\([2]\)): \(C_2 \cong C_1 \times_{C_0} C_1\), ensuring sequential corporate couplings compose associatively up to coherent homotopy.

§5.3.2–5.3.3: Syntroclinic Bridge Proof & Postnikov Contraction \(\tau_{\le m}\)

STRATUM B: BRIDGE LIFTING PROOF (DEF. 5.7, PROP. 5.8, FIG. 5.3) & POSTNIKOV CONTRACTION (DEF. 5.9, PROP. 5.10, FIG. 5.4)

Definition 5.7 & Proposition 5.8: Syntroclinic Bridge Adjunction For grades \(n \ge 0\) and \(N \ge 1\), the Syntroclinic Bridge is the left adjoint extension-of-scalars functor: \[ B_{n, n+N} \;\coloneqq\; (\phi_{n, n+N})_! \colon \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn) \;\rightleftarrows\; \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_{n+N}}(\Xsyn) \;\colon (\phi_{n, n+N})^* =: R_{n+N, n} \] On the subcategory \(\mathcal{I}_n \subseteq \Met_n(\Xsyn)\) of invariant syndromes, the restricted bridge \(B_{n, n+N}|_{\mathcal{I}_n}\) is fully faithful if and only if for every \(X \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathcal{I}_n)\), the adjunction unit is an equivalence in \(\Met_n(\Xsyn)\): \[ \eta_X \colon X \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; R_{n+N, n}\big(B_{n, n+N}(X)\big) \]

Proof of Proposition 5.8 (Standard Adjunction Criterion for Fully Faithful Lifting): For any \(X, Y \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathcal{I}_n)\), the adjunction \(B_{n, n+N} \dashv R_{n+N, n}\) provides a natural homotopy equivalence of mapping spaces: \[ \Map_{\Alg_{\mathcal{O}_{n+N}}}\!\big(B_{n, n+N}(X),\, B_{n, n+N}(Y)\big) \;\simeq\; \Map_{\Alg_{\On}}\!\big(X,\, R_{n+N, n}(B_{n, n+N}(Y))\big) \] Under this equivalence, the action of \(B_{n, n+N}\) on mapping spaces \(\Map(X, Y) \to \Map(B(X), B(Y))\) factors as post-composition with the unit morphism \((\eta_Y)_* \colon \Map(X, Y) \to \Map(X, R(B(Y)))\). By the Yoneda Lemma in \((\infty, 1)\)-categories (Lurie 2009, §5.1.3), \((\eta_Y)_*\) is a homotopy equivalence for all \(X \in \mathcal{I}_n\) iff \(\eta_Y \colon Y \xrightarrow{\sim} R_{n+N, n}(B_{n, n+N}(Y))\) is an equivalence. \(\blacksquare\)

Definition 5.11: Bisimplicial Tectonic Object \(\Tect(\mathcal{S})\) For an associative Metroplex \(\mathcal{S} \in \Met_n(\Xsyn)\), its dual endogenous architecture is realized as a bisimplicial object: \[ \Tect(\mathcal{S}) \;\in\; \operatorname{Fun}\big(\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \times \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}},\; \Xsyn\big) \] with commuting vertical face/degeneracy operators (\(d_i^v, s_i^v\) on \(\operatorname{Gr}_\bullet\), grades \(0 \le k \le n-1\)) and horizontal operators (\(d_j^h, s_j^h\) on \(\operatorname{Syn}_\bullet\), syndrome layers).

Definition 5.12: Homological Banach Realization Functor \(\RBan\) On \(\Xsyn^{\mathrm{coord}} \subseteq \Xsyn\) (sheaves \(X\) with finitely generated total homology of \(\Gamma(X)\) and basis \(B_X\)), via free \(\mathbb{R}\)-linearization \(\mathbb{R}[-] \colon \mathcal{S} \to s\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}}\) and Dold–Kan normalization \(N_\bullet \colon s\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathbf{Ch}_{\ge 0}(\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})\): \[ \RBan(X) \;\coloneqq\; \bigoplus_{k=0}^\infty H_k\!\Big( N_\bullet\big(\mathbb{R}[\Gamma(X)]\big) \Big)_{\ell^1} \;\in\; \operatorname{Obj}(\FinBan) \] Degree \(k=0\) recovers \(H_0 \cong \mathbb{R}[\pi_0(\Gamma(X))]\), while \(k \ge 1\) preserves higher homotopical invariants, yielding \(\Tect_{\mathbf{Ban}}(\mathcal{S}) \coloneqq \RBan \circ \Tect(\mathcal{S})\).

Theorem 5.13: Tectonic 2-Fold Segal Realization Theorem Pre-composing with \(\operatorname{diag} \colon \mathbf{\Delta} \to \mathbf{\Delta} \times \mathbf{\Delta}\) (\([k] \mapsto \Tect(\mathcal{S})_{k,k}\)) yields the Total Tectonic Object: \[ \big|\Tect(\mathcal{S})\big|_{\mathbf{\Delta}} \;\coloneqq\; \colim_{\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}}\big(\operatorname{diag}^* \Tect(\mathcal{S})\big) \;\simeq\; \colim_{\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \times \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}} \Tect(\mathcal{S})_{p,q} \] unifying vertical gradual and horizontal syndromatic architectures into a single coherent homotopy type in \(\Xsyn\).

Proof of Theorem 5.15 (Eilenberg–Zilber & Spectral Convergence): By the Eilenberg–Zilber–Cartier Theorem, \(N_\bullet(\operatorname{diag}^*\Tect_{\mathbf{Ban}}(\mathcal{S})) \simeq \operatorname{Tot}(C_{\bullet,\bullet}(\mathcal{S}))\) with \(D = \partial^{\mathrm{grad}} + (-1)^p \partial^{\mathrm{syn}}\). Since \(C_{p,q} = 0\) for \(p < 0\) or \(q < 0\), the column filtration \(F_p\operatorname{Tot}_m = \bigoplus_{i \le p} C_{i, m-i}\) is bounded below and exhaustive, guaranteeing finite-stage convergence \(E^\infty_{p,q} \cong \operatorname{Gr}_p H_{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot})\) (Mac Lane 1998). A non-vanishing differential \(d^r \ne 0\) (\(r \ge 2\)) is the exact homological obstruction to lifting a gradual \(p\)-cycle across \(r\) vertical grades without modifying syndrome level by \(r-1\) (Metroplexdiabatik, SM p. 103). \(\blacksquare\)

Carnap 5.1 (Scale-Relativity & Resolving Kim’s Downward Causation): Within Ontic Structural Realism (Ladyman & Ross 2007; French 2014), Theorem 5.15 and \((\phi_{n,n+N})_! \dashv (\phi_{n,n+N})^*\) dissolve Jaegwon Kim’s causal exclusion paradox: macro-scale constraint is not an anomalous force violating grade-\(0\) dynamics, but the transgression differential \(d^r\) and right-adjoint restriction \((\phi_{n,n+N})^*\) selecting globally compatible cohomology classes in \(\operatorname{Tot}(C_{\bullet,\bullet})\).

Definition 5.16: State Totality & Grade-\(n\) Slice Category \(T_n\) For a generative blueprint object \(G_n \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Met_n(\Xsyn))\), the structured realization category of grade-\(n\) state totality \(\mathsf{Tot}_n\) is the slice category: \[ T_n \;\coloneqq\; \Met_n(\Xsyn) / G_n \] * Terminal Object: \(\operatorname{id}_{G_n} \colon G_n \to G_n\). * Initial Object (Nullmetroplex \({}^n\mathbf{M}_0\)): \((0_n \to G_n)\) modeling structural exhaustion.

Definition 5.17: Augmented Subobject-Minimal Protosimplex Let \(\Alg_{\On}^0\) be the category of augmented algebras over the base constant subalgebra \(\Free_{\On}(\emptyset)\). An object \(\mathcal{P} \in \operatorname{Obj}(T_n)\) is a Protosimplex of Grade \(n\) if \(\mathcal{P} \not\cong \Free_{\On}(\emptyset)\) and it has no proper non-trivial augmented sub-algebras: \[ \forall A \hookrightarrow \mathcal{P} \text{ in } \Alg_{\On}^0, \qquad A \cong \Free_{\On}(\emptyset) \quad \lor \quad A \cong \mathcal{P} \]

Definition 5.18: Endogenous Synthesis (\(\SynEN\)) & Absorption (\(\AbsEN\)) \[ \SynEN_{p,q}^n \colon \Met_p(\Xsyn) \times \Met_q(\Xsyn) \longrightarrow \Met_n(\Xsyn) \qquad (p + q = n,\; q > 0) \] \[ \AbsEN_n^{p+q} \colon \Met_n(\Xsyn) \times \Met_{p+q}(\Xsyn) \longrightarrow \Met_n(\Xsyn) \qquad (p + q \le n,\; q > 0) \] Strict inequality \(p + q \le n\) prevents infinite recursive runaway during combination.

import Mathlib
open CategoryTheory
namespace Syntrometrie.StratumA.Metroplex

/-- Endogenous combination grade-admissibility (SM Eq. 26, Def. 5.18) -/
structure EndogenousAdmissible (n p q : ℕ) : Prop where
  grade_bound : p + q ≤ n
  pos_shift   : 0 < q

/-- Syntroclinic bridge hom-set adjunction equivalence (Def. 5.7, Prop. 5.8) -/
def syntroclinicHomEquiv {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D]
    {B : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : B ⊣ R) (X : C) (Y : D) :
    (B.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X ⟶ R.obj Y) :=
  adj.homEquiv X Y
end Syntrometrie.StratumA.Metroplex

1. Basepoint-Preserving Telecentric Path Signature \(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}\) (Def. 6.6) In the locally presentable category of diffeological spaces \(\mathbf{Diff}_{\mathrm{smooth}}\) (Souriau 1980; Iglesias-Zemmour 2013), fix step \(\epsilon > 0\): \[ \mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}(M) \;\coloneqq\; \Big( M \times C^\infty\big([0, \epsilon], M\big) \Big)_{\operatorname{ev}_0 = \operatorname{pr}_1} \;\amalg\; \mathbf{1} \] where \(\operatorname{ev}_0(\gamma) = \gamma(0) = x\) enforces basepoint continuity and \(\mathbf{1} = \{\ast_{\mathrm{term}}\}\) models \(\nullsyntrix\).

2. Proof of Theorem 6.7 (Existence of Final Coalgebra \((\nu\mathcal{T}, \zeta)\)) Since \(C^\infty([0,\epsilon], -)\) is a representable hom-functor in cartesian closed \(\mathbf{Diff}_{\mathrm{smooth}}\), it preserves connected limits; finite products and coproducts with \(\mathbf{1}\) commute with \(\omega^{\mathrm{op}}\)-limits. Thus the Adámek–Aczel terminal sequence \(\mathbf{1} \leftarrow \mathcal{T}\mathbf{1} \leftarrow \mathcal{T}^2\mathbf{1} \leftarrow \cdots\) stabilizes at \(\omega\): \(\nu\mathcal{T} \coloneqq \lim_{k<\omega}\mathcal{T}^k(\mathbf{1})\) carries a unique universal mediating arrow \(!_\alpha \colon S \to \nu\mathcal{T}\) for every \((S, \alpha)\). \(\blacksquare\)

3. Proof of Proposition 6.8 (Banach Fixed Point & Lambek Isomorphism) For any \((S, \alpha)\), the cone maps \(\alpha_k \colon S \to \mathcal{T}^k(\mathbf{1})\) (\(\alpha_{k+1} = \mathcal{T}(\alpha_k) \circ \alpha\)) induce the unique fixed point \(!_\alpha = \zeta^{-1} \circ \mathcal{T}(!_\alpha) \circ \alpha\). Regarding \((\mathcal{T}\nu\mathcal{T}, \mathcal{T}\zeta)\) as a coalgebra yields \(\eta \colon \mathcal{T}\nu\mathcal{T} \to \nu\mathcal{T}\) with \(\zeta\eta = \mathcal{T}(\eta\zeta)\). Since \(\zeta\) is a coalgebra map, \(\eta\zeta = \operatorname{id}_{\nu\mathcal{T}}\) by finality, so \(\zeta\eta = \mathcal{T}(\operatorname{id}) = \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{T}\nu\mathcal{T}}\). \(\blacksquare\)

4. Carnap 6.1: Eliminating Retrocausal Metaphysics Two states \(x_1, x_2 \in S\) are telecentrically equivalent iff \(!_\alpha(x_1) = !_\alpha(x_2)\) in \(\nu\mathcal{T}\). Combined with Friston/Clark free-energy dissipation, Telezentrik is completely reduced to forward differential geometry and coalgebraic behavioral equivalence!

import Mathlib
open CategoryTheory
namespace Syntrometrie.StratumB.Telezentrik

structure Coalgebra (T : C ⥤ C) where
  carrier : C
  str     : carrier ⟶ T.obj carrier

/-- Final Telecentric Coalgebra (νT, ζ) certifying unique mediating arrow !ₐ (Thm. 6.7) -/
structure FinalCoalgebra (T : C ⥤ C) where
  terminal   : Coalgebra T
  toTerminal : (S : Coalgebra T) → (S.carrier ⟶ terminal.carrier)
  comm       : ∀ S, S.str ≫ T.map (toTerminal S) = toTerminal S ≫ terminal.str
  uniq       : ∀ (S : Coalgebra T) (f : S.carrier ⟶ terminal.carrier),
                 S.str ≫ T.map f = f ≫ terminal.str → f = toTerminal S
end Syntrometrie.StratumB.Telezentrik

Definition 6.9 & Theorem 6.10: Strict Televariant Stability Theorem Let \(\mathcal{K}_c = \{V(x) \le c\} \subset \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A})\) be a compact sublevel set of excess potential \(V(x) \coloneqq \Psi(x) - \Psi(\mathcal{A})\) satisfying: 1. Morse–Bott Quadratic Coercivity: \(V(x) \ge \frac{\mu}{2}\dist_{\gAR}(x, \mathcal{A})^2\) (\(\mu > 0\)). 2. Polyak–Łojasiewicz (PL) Gradient Dissipation: \(\dot{V}(x) = \mathcal{L}_{\XAR}V(x) \le -\gamma V(x)\) (\(\gamma > 0\)). Then \(\mathcal{K}_c\) is positively invariant and every televariant trajectory \(x_0 \in \mathcal{K}_c\) converges exponentially to the Telezentrum \(\mathcal{A}\): \[ \dist_{\gAR}\big(\Phi_t(x_0), \mathcal{A}\big) \;\le\; \sqrt{\frac{2V(x_0)}{\mu}}\, e^{-\frac{\gamma}{2}t} \;\xrightarrow{t\to\infty}\; 0 \]

Proof of Theorem 6.10 (Grönwall & Metric Coercivity Bound): Along any integral curve \(x(t) = \Phi_t(x_0)\) with \(x_0 \in \mathcal{K}_c\), \(\frac{d}{dt}V(x(t)) = \mathcal{L}_{\XAR}V(x(t)) \le -\gamma V(x(t)) \le 0\), so \(V(x(t)) \le V(x_0) \le c\) and \(x(t)\) remains in \(\mathcal{K}_c\) for all \(t \ge 0\). Multiplying by \(e^{\gamma t}\) gives \(\frac{d}{dt}[e^{\gamma t}V(x(t))] \le 0\), which integrates by Grönwall’s Lemma to \(V(\Phi_t(x_0)) \le V(x_0)e^{-\gamma t}\). Combining with Morse–Bott quadratic coercivity \(\frac{\mu}{2}\dist_{\gAR}(\Phi_t(x_0), \mathcal{A})^2 \le V(\Phi_t(x_0))\) and taking square roots yields the exact exponential decay rate \(\gamma/2\). \(\blacksquare\)

Remark (Toy Example: 1D Double-Well Telecentric Potential): On \(\MAR = \mathbb{R}\) with \(\Psi(x) = (x^2 - 1)^2\) and \(\dot{x} = -\Psi'(x) = -4x(x^2 - 1)\), the critical set \(\Crit(\Psi) = \{-1, 0, +1\}\) splits into two stable Punkttelezentren \(T_{z,1} = -1\), \(T_{z,2} = +1\) (\(\Psi''(\pm 1) = 8 > 0\)) with televariant basins \((-\infty, 0)\) and \((0, +\infty)\), separated by the unstable saddle \(p_0 = 0\) (\(\Psi''(0) = -4 < 0\)) forming the Extinktionsdiskriminante \(\Dext = \{0\}\).

Theorem 6.13 (Telecentre Dimension Bounds & Foliation, SM pp. 117–118): In an \(n\)-dimensional Tensorium, every Telezentrum satisfies \(0 \le \gamma_k \le n - 1\): * Equal Dimensions (\(\gamma_1 = \gamma_2\)): Connected by a unique Telezentrale of dimension \(\gamma_1 + 1\). * Unequal Dimensions (\(\gamma_2 > \gamma_1\)): Connected by a \((\gamma_2 - \gamma_1)\)-parameter family of \((\gamma_1 + 1)\)-dimensional Telezentralen foliating a region of dimension \(\gamma_2 + 1\).

Theorem 6.14 & Proof (Morse–Smale Stratified Separatrix Boundary Theorem): For a Morse–Smale gradient system \(\XAR = -\grad_{\gAR}\Psi\) on compact \((\MAR, \gAR)\), the Extinktionsdiskriminante \(\Dext \coloneqq \partial\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A})\) is the Whitney-stratified union of stable manifolds of hyperbolic saddles \(p_r \in \Crit(\Psi)\) of Morse index \(\ind(p_r) \ge 1\): \[ \Dext \;=\; \overline{\bigcup_{\ind(p_j)=1} W^s(p_j)} \;=\; \bigcup_{r \,:\, \ind(p_r)\ge 1} W^s(p_r), \qquad \dim W^s(p_j) = n - 1 \] Proof: By the Stable Manifold Theorem for Morse–Smale gradient flows (Palis & de Melo 1982), \(\MAR = \bigsqcup_{p \in \Crit(\Psi)} W^s(p)\) where \(\operatorname{codim} W^s(p) = \ind(p)\). Open basins \(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A}_k)\) are unions of index-\(0\) stable manifolds; their topological boundary \(\partial\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A})\) is invariant and must consist of stable manifolds of codimension \(\ge 1\) (\(\ind(p_r) \ge 1\)). By the \(\lambda\)-Lemma (Inclination Lemma), transversality \(W^u(p_r) \pitchfork W^s(p_j)\) guarantees that the frontier \(\overline{W^s(p_j)} \setminus W^s(p_j)\) is a Whitney-stratified union of higher-index stable manifolds \(W^s(p_r)\) (\(\ind(p_r) \ge 2\)). \(\blacksquare\)

Theorem 6.16 (Branching Types of Extinction Boundary, SM pp. 113–114): Initial and final dysvariance correspond to a single-branch extinction boundary \(\Dext\), whereas intermittent dysvariance corresponds to a two-branch boundary enclosing a metastable recovery zone where Resynkolation restores televariance!

Definition 6.15 & Theorem 6.19: Transzendente Telezentralenrelativität Let \(\mathbf{Trans}\) be the hierarchy of transcendence strata \(C(m)\) modeled by coalgebra categories \(\mathcal{C}_m \coloneqq \Coalg(\mathcal{T}_m)\) with terminal Telezentrum \((\nu\mathcal{T}_m, \zeta_m)\). The Transzendenzsynkolator \(\Gamma_m \colon \mathcal{C}_m \to \mathcal{C}_{m+1}\) is left adjoint to the forgetful functor \(U_{m+1}\): \[ \Gamma_m \;\dashv\; U_{m+1} \colon \Coalg(\mathcal{T}_{m+1}) \longrightarrow \Coalg(\mathcal{T}_m) \] Under this adjunction, the terminal Haupttelezentrum of stratum \(C(m)\) is mapped to a non-terminal basal Nebentelezentrum in \(C(m+1)\): \[ \boxed{\Gamma_m(\nu\mathcal{T}_m) \;\cong\; \HypMet_{m+1} \;\not\cong\; \nu\mathcal{T}_{m+1} \quad\text{in }\mathcal{C}_{m+1}} \]

Proof of Theorem 6.19 (Left-Adjoint Non-Preservation of Terminal Coalgebras): 1. Basal Lifting: In stratum \(\mathcal{C}_m\), every televariant system \((S_m, \alpha_m)\) admits a unique coalgebra homomorphism \(!_{\alpha_m} \colon S_m \to \nu\mathcal{T}_m\). 2. Transcendence Encapsulation: Applying the Transzendenzsynkolator \(\Gamma_m \colon \mathcal{C}_m \to \mathcal{C}_{m+1}\) encapsulates the stabilized terminal invariants \(\nu\mathcal{T}_m\) as the initial free generator \(\HypMet_{m+1} \coloneqq \Gamma_m(\nu\mathcal{T}_m)\) of the higher-order coalgebra category \(\mathcal{C}_{m+1}\). 3. Categorical Relativity: By general category theory (Mac Lane 1998), left adjoints preserve colimits and initial objects, but do not preserve terminal objects or final coalgebras. Since \(\Gamma_m(\nu\mathcal{T}_m)\) is an initial generator in \(\mathcal{C}_{m+1}\) while \(\nu\mathcal{T}_{m+1}\) is terminal, \(\Gamma_m(\nu\mathcal{T}_m) \not\cong \nu\mathcal{T}_{m+1}\) whenever \(\mathcal{C}_{m+1}\) is non-degenerate. \(\blacksquare\)

Definition 7.3 (Category \(\Ctxquant\)) & Definition 7.4 (Realization Functor \(U_{\mathrm{quant}}\)): * Objects \(U_Q \coloneqq (U, n_U, \mathbb{K}_U, \rho_U)\): \(U \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathbf{Ctx}_{\mathrm{adm}}^{\mathrm{sk}})\), field \(\mathbb{K}_U \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Coeff)\), and norm-preserving \(\mathbb{Q}\)-algebra representation \(\rho_U \colon \mathbb{K}_U \to \mathcal{L}(P^U)\) equipping the Predicatrix carrier: \[ U_{\mathrm{quant}}(U_Q) \;\coloneqq\; P^U \;\cong\; (\mathbb{K}_U^{n_U})_{\mathbb{R}} \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{R}^3 \;\cong\; \mathbb{R}^{3 d(\mathbb{K}_U) n_U} \] such that \(z^U \in \operatorname{Isom}_{\mathbb{K}_U}(P^U)\) commutes with \(\rho_U(\mathbb{K}_U)\). * Morphisms \(\alpha \colon U_Q \to V_Q\): Context morphism \(\alpha = (\alpha_D, \alpha_P, \alpha_C)\) with subfield inclusion \(\iota \colon \mathbb{K}_U \hookrightarrow \mathbb{K}_V\) intertwining scalar actions and preserving cipher subspaces: \[ \alpha_P \circ \rho_U(\lambda) = \rho_V(\iota(\lambda)) \circ \alpha_P \quad (\forall \lambda \in \mathbb{K}_U), \qquad z^V(\operatorname{Im}(\alpha_P)) \subseteq \operatorname{Im}(\alpha_P) \]

Proposition 7.5 & Proof (Well-Definedness & Pullback Completeness of \(\Ctxquant\)): \(\Ctxquant\) is a well-defined category with all finite pullbacks, the forgetful functor \(I \colon \Ctxquant \to \mathbf{Ctx}_{\mathrm{adm}}^{\mathrm{sk}}\) strictly preserves pullbacks, and \(U_{\mathrm{quant}} \colon \Ctxquant \to \mathbf{Ban}_{\le 1}\) is contractive.

Proof: Composition intertwines via \((\beta_P\circ\alpha_P)\circ\rho_U(\lambda) = \rho_W((\iota_2\circ\iota_1)(\lambda))\circ(\beta_P\circ\alpha_P)\). Given a cospan \(V_{1,Q} \xrightarrow{\alpha} U_Q \xleftarrow{\beta} V_{2,Q}\), set \(\mathbb{K}_W \coloneqq \mathbb{K}_{V_1} \cap \mathbb{K}_{V_2} = \min(\mathbb{K}_{V_1}, \mathbb{K}_{V_2}) \in \Coeff\). On the pullback context \(W = V_1 \times_U V_2\), define \(\rho_W(\lambda)(p_1, p_2) \coloneqq (\rho_{V_1}(\lambda)p_1, \rho_{V_2}(\lambda)p_2)\) for \(\lambda \in \mathbb{K}_W\). Whenever \(\alpha_P(p_1) = \beta_P(p_2)\), intertwining gives \(\alpha_P(\rho_{V_1}(\lambda)p_1) = \rho_U(\lambda)(\alpha_P(p_1)) = \rho_U(\lambda)(\beta_P(p_2)) = \beta_P(\rho_{V_2}(\lambda)p_2)\), so \(P^W \subset P^{V_1}\oplus_\infty P^{V_2}\) is closed under \(\rho_W(\mathbb{K}_W)\), yielding a universal pullback strictly preserved by \(I\). \(\blacksquare\)

1. Triadic Predicatrix Carrier \(P^U \cong \mathbb{R}^{3 d(\mathbb{K}_U) n_U}\) (Defs. 7.3–7.4):
Why the factor of \(3\)? Each quantitative coordinate \(l \in \{1, \dots, n_U\}\) carries a realified \(\mathbb{K}_U\)-fiber \((\mathbb{K}_U)_{\mathbb{R}} \cong \mathbb{R}^{d(\mathbb{K}_U)}\) tensored with the 3-dimensional syntrometric predicate space \(\mathbb{R}^3\) (affirmation, negation, and dialectical synthesis), while isometric cipher \(z^U \in \operatorname{Isom}_{\mathbb{K}_U}(P^U)\) commutes with \(\rho_U(\mathbb{K}_U)\).
2. Semilinear Intertwining Across Subfield Inclusions (Def. 7.3):
When a context refinement \(\alpha \colon U_Q \to V_Q\) extends scalars along \(\iota \colon \mathbb{K}_U \hookrightarrow \mathbb{K}_V\) (e.g., \(\mathbb{R} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}\)), the Banach contraction \(\alpha_P \colon P^U \to P^V\) satisfies \(\alpha_P(\rho_U(\lambda)p) = \rho_V(\iota(\lambda))\alpha_P(p)\) and cipher invariance \(z^V(\operatorname{Im}(\alpha_P)) \subseteq \operatorname{Im}(\alpha_P)\).
3. Complete Lattice Meet in \(\Coeff\) Ensures Pullback Stability (Prop. 7.5):
Because \(\Coeff = [\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R} \subseteq \mathbb{C}]\) is a finite total order, any cospan \(\mathbb{K}_{V_1} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{K}_U \hookleftarrow \mathbb{K}_{V_2}\) has an exact pullback \(\mathbb{K}_W = \mathbb{K}_{V_1} \cap \mathbb{K}_{V_2} = \min(\mathbb{K}_{V_1}, \mathbb{K}_{V_2})\) on which \(\rho_W = \rho_{V_1} \times \rho_{V_2}\) restricts cleanly to the fiber product \(P^W \subset P^{V_1} \oplus_\infty P^{V_2}\).

§7.2.2: Bounded Tensor Spaces & Colored Operad \(\Oquant\)

STRATUM A: DEFINITIONS 7.10–7.12 & TENSOR OPERAD ACTION RIBBON (FIG. 7.3) | STAGE S₁b

Def. 7.10 (Scalar vs. Tensorial Products) & Def. 7.11 (Banach Tensor Spaces): * Def. 7.10 (SM, p. 128): In the \(\quantitaetsaspekt\), the scalar product \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\) contracts directional data to a scalar, whereas the tensorial product retains directional information in a tensor-valued result (not restricted to the 3D cross product). * Def. 7.11 (Bounded Continuous Tensor Fields): Over a smooth \(m\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold \((R_m, g_m)\), let \(T^{\otimes k}R_m\) be the pure contravariant rank-\(k\) tensor bundle with fiberwise norm \(\|\cdot\|_{g_m}\). The space: \[ X_{(m,k)} \;\coloneqq\; \Gamma_b^0(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m) \;=\; \left\{ A \in \Gamma(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m) \;\middle|\; \|A\|_{C_b^0} \coloneqq \sup_{y \in R_m}\|A(y)\|_{g_m} < \infty \right\} \] is a real Banach space (Ryan 2002).

Definition 7.12 (Colored Operad \(\Oquant\) & Isometric Suboperad \(\Oisom\)): With colors \(\mathbf{Col}_{\mathrm{tensor}} \coloneqq \{(m, k) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}_0\}\), the \(\mathsf{Ban}\)-enriched colored operad \(\Oquant\) has: 1. Operation Spaces: Bounded multilinear operators under the projective cross-norm \(\widehat{\otimes}_\pi\): \[ \Oquant\big((m_1, k_1), \dots, (m_r, k_r);\; (m, k)\big) \;\coloneqq\; \mathcal{B}\!\left(X_{(m_1, k_1)} \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi X_{(m_r, k_r)},\; X_{(m, k)}\right) \] with \(\|f\|_{\mathrm{op}} \coloneqq \sup_{\|A_i\|\le 1}\|f(A_1, \dots, A_r)\|_{C_b^0}\) and identity \(\operatorname{id}_{(m,k)}\). 2. Operadic Substitution: \(\gamma(f; g_1, \dots, g_r) \coloneqq f \circ (g_1 \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi g_r)\) extends contractively via the universal property of \(\widehat{\otimes}_\pi\). 3. Isometric Natural Suboperad \(\Oisom \subseteq \Oquant\): Single-base operations equivariant under the isometry Lie group \(G_m = \operatorname{Isom}(R_m, g_m)\): \[ f(\varphi_* A_1, \dots, \varphi_* A_r) = \varphi_* f(A_1, \dots, A_r) \quad \forall \varphi \in G_m \]

§7.3.1: Dimensional Parameter Functor \(S_n\) & Continuous Metropie Flow

STRATUM B: DERIVED CONSTRUCTIONS — DEFINITION 7.13 & LIE GROUP METROPIE FLOW (FIG. 7.4)

Definition 7.13 (Category \(\DimField\) and Dimensional Parameter Functor \(S_n\)): Let \(\DimField\) be the category whose: * Objects: Pairs \((\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda})\) where \(\mathbb{K} \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Coeff)\) and \(\mathbf{\Lambda} = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)\) is a positive diagonal scaling matrix (\(\lambda_l > 0\) encoding physical units). * Morphisms: Scale-contractive inclusions \(\iota \colon (\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda}) \to (\mathbb{L}, \mathbf{\Lambda}')\) satisfying \(\lambda'_l \|\iota(x)\|_{\mathbb{L}} \le \lambda_l \|x\|_{\mathbb{K}}\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{K}\) (\(1 \le l \le n\)). * Dimensional Parameter Functor \(S_n \colon \DimField \to \mathbf{Ban}_{\le 1}\): Assigns to \((\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda})\) the realified parameter space \(R_n \coloneqq (\mathbb{K}^n)_{\mathbb{R}} \cong \mathbb{R}^{d(\mathbb{K})n}\) equipped with the weighted norm: \[ \|y\|_{R_n} \;\coloneqq\; \max_{1 \le l \le n} \lambda_l \|y_l\|_{\mathbb{K}} \] and maps morphisms to \(\widetilde{\iota} \colon R_n(\mathbb{K}) \to R_n(\mathbb{L})\) with \(S_n(\operatorname{id}) = \operatorname{id}_{R_n}\) and \(S_n(\iota_2 \circ \iota_1) = S_n(\iota_2) \circ S_n(\iota_1)\).

Continuous Metropie Flow on the Lie Group of Isometric Ciphers (Fig. 7.4): On realified carriers \(P^U\), orientation-preserving isometric ciphers form the compact Lie group \(\operatorname{Isom}^+(P^U) \cong \mathrm{SO}(n)\) with Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{so}(n)\). A continuous Metropie transition \(\gamma(t) = z(t) \in \mathrm{SO}(n)\) from \(z(0) = z^U\) to \(z(1) = z^V\) carries the positive-definite Killing–Cartan metric tensor: \[ g_{\mathrm{met}}(\dot{z}, \dot{z}) \coloneqq -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left((z^{-1}\dot{z}) \circ (z^{-1}\dot{z})\right) \ge 0, \qquad d_{\mathbf{Ctx}}(U, V) \le \int_0^1 \sqrt{g_{\mathrm{met}}(\dot{\gamma}, \dot{\gamma})}\,dt \]

§7.3.2: Geometry of Synkolatorraum: Isocline Foliations & Morse–Bott Centers

STRATUM B: SCHOLIUM 7.14, DEFINITION 7.15, TOY EXAMPLE & CORNERS FOLIATION (FIG. 7.5)

Scholium 7.14 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Isocline Foliations & Field Centers): Differential topology reconstructs Heim’s intuitive geometric contours (Isoklinen) and focal extrema (Feldzentren, SM pp. 129–130) with coordinate-free rigor: 1. Regular Isoclines as Foliations: By the constant-rank submersion theorem on \(R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}\), level sets \(\Sigma_c = ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c)\) are embedded submanifolds of codimension \(d\) forming a regular foliation \(\mathfrak{f}_A\). 2. Feldzentren as Morse–Bott Submanifolds: Extrema of \(\Phi(A) = \|A\|_{g_m}^2\) form the critical locus \(d(\Phi\circ A) = 0\), decomposing under Morse–Bott regularity into disjoint smooth critical submanifolds \(\bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha\).

Definition 7.15 (Synkolatorraum \(\Msyn\), Submersion Foliation \(\mathfrak{f}_A\) & Field Centers \(Z_\alpha\)): 1. Synkolatorraum: Total space \(\Msyn \coloneqq T^{\otimes k}R_m\) with \(\dim(\Msyn) = m + m^k\). 2. Regular Locus & Foliation: For smooth component map \({}^m\bar{A} \colon R_m \to \mathbb{R}^d\) (\(d \le m\)), \[ R_m^{\mathrm{reg}} \coloneqq \big\{y \in R_m \;\big|\; \operatorname{rank}(d({}^m\bar{A})_y) = d\big\}, \qquad \Sigma_c \coloneqq ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c) \cap R_m^{\mathrm{reg}} \] Connected components of \(\Sigma_c\) form a smooth codimension-\(d\) foliation \(\mathfrak{f}_A\) on \(R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}\). 3. Critical Field Centers: For \(\Phi(A) \coloneqq \|A\|_{g_m}^2\), \(Z(A, g_m, \Phi) \coloneqq \{y \in R_m \mid d(\Phi\circ A)_y = 0\} = \bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha\) (\(\dim Z_\alpha = d_\alpha \le m\)).

Remark (Toy Example: 2D Parameter Space with Concentric Isoclines): On \(R_2 = \mathbb{R}^2\) (\(g = \delta_{ij}\)) with scalar field (\(k=0\)) \(f(y_1, y_2) = y_1^2 + y_2^2\): \(\Msyn = R_2 \times \mathbb{R}^1 \cong \mathbb{R}^3\); regular locus \(R_2^{\mathrm{reg}} = \mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{(0,0)\}\) since \(df = (2y_1, 2y_2) \ne (0,0)\); Isoclines \(\Sigma_c = \{y_1^2 + y_2^2 = c\}\) (\(c>0\)) are concentric circles of radius \(\sqrt{c}\); Field Center \(Z = \{(0,0)\}\) (Fehlstelle \(\mathbf{0}\) in Fig. 7.5) is an isolated 0D Morse minimum.

§7.3.3: Layered Processing Cascade, Initial Section \(A_0\) & Musical Pullbacks

STRATUM B: DEFINITION 7.16, PROPOSITION 7.17 & STRUKTURKASKADE PIPELINE (FIG. 7.6)

Definition 7.16 (Canonical Coordinate Frame Initial Section \(A_0\)): Let \(\pi_1 \colon R_n \to R_{m_1}\) project onto the active \(m_1\)-dimensional subspace (\(m_1 \le n\)), and let \(X_0 \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_1}, TR_{m_1})\). The canonical reference section \(A_0 \in X_0\) is the normalized coordinate frame vector field: \[ A_0(y) \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{m_1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y_i}}{\left\|\sum_{i=1}^{m_1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y_i}\right\|_{g(y)}}, \qquad \|A_0(y)\|_{g(y)} = 1 \;\implies\; \|A_0\|_{C_b^0} = 1 \] grounding the tensor cascade strictly in the unit ball of continuous sections. The first syndrome section is generated by \(f_1 \in \Oquant(r_1)\): \[ A_1 \;\coloneqq\; f_1(A_0, \dots, A_0) \;\in\; X_1 \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_1}, T^{\otimes k_1}R_{m_1}) \]

Proposition 7.17 (Well-Typed Layered Cascade via Contravariant Musical Pullbacks): Let \(X_\gamma \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_\gamma}, T^{\otimes k_\gamma}R_{m_\gamma})\) (\(1 \le \gamma \le M\)). Because contravariant tensors push forward rather than pull back directly along Riemannian submersions \(\pi_\gamma \colon R_{m_\gamma} \to R_{m_{\gamma-1}}\) (\(\|d\pi_\gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1\)), define the Contravariant Musical Pullback \(\pi_\gamma^\circledast\) via the metric musical isomorphisms \(\flat_g \colon TR \xrightarrow{\sim} T^*R\) and \(\sharp_g \colon T^*R \xrightarrow{\sim} TR\): \[ \pi_\gamma^\circledast(A) \;\coloneqq\; \sharp_{g_{m_\gamma}}^{\otimes k_{\gamma-1}} \circ \pi_\gamma^* \circ \flat_{g_{m_{\gamma-1}}}^{\otimes k_{\gamma-1}}(A), \qquad \big\|\pi_\gamma^\circledast(A)\big\|_{C_b^0} \;\le\; \|A\|_{C_b^0} \] Then \(X_0 \xrightarrow{f_1} X_1 \xrightarrow{f_2} \dots \xrightarrow{f_M} X_M\) is a strictly well-typed contractive cascade via \(f_\gamma \circ (\pi_\gamma^\circledast)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi r_\gamma} \colon X_{\gamma-1}^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi r_\gamma} \to X_\gamma\).

Interactive 4-Tab Inspector: Musical Pullbacks & Layered Cascade Typing

1. Why Normalize \(A_0\) to \(\|A_0\|_{C_b^0} = 1\)? (Def. 7.16):
A raw coordinate frame \(\sum \partial/\partial y_i\) has metric norm \(\sqrt{m_1}\) on flat space and can vary wildly on curved manifolds. Normalizing pointwise by \(\|\sum \partial/\partial y_i\|_{g(y)}\) guarantees \(\|A_0\|_{C_b^0} = 1\), anchoring the entire recursive Strukturkaskade on the unit sphere of \(X_0\).
2. Why Musical Isomorphisms Are Required Across Submanifolds (Prop. 7.17):
Smooth maps \(\pi_\gamma \colon R_{m_\gamma} \to R_{m_{\gamma-1}}\) natively pull back covariant forms (\(\pi_\gamma^*\)), not contravariant tensors \(T^{\otimes k}\). Lowering indices via \(\flat_{g_{m_{\gamma-1}}}^{\otimes k}\), pulling back via \(\pi_\gamma^*\), and raising indices via \(\sharp_{g_{m_\gamma}}^{\otimes k}\) resolves the variance mismatch canonically.
3. Contractivity of \(\pi_\gamma^\circledast\) Under Riemannian Submersions:
Since \(\flat_g\) and \(\sharp_g\) are fiberwise isometries (\(\|\flat_g\|_{\mathrm{op}} = \|\sharp_g\|_{\mathrm{op}} = 1\)) and \(\|d\pi_\gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1\), the composite \(\pi_\gamma^\circledast\) satisfies \(\|\pi_\gamma^\circledast(A)\|_{C_b^0} \le \|d\pi_\gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k_{\gamma-1}} \|A\|_{C_b^0} \le \|A\|_{C_b^0}\).
4. Hierarchical Syndrome Pipeline (Fig. 7.6):
\(R_n \xrightarrow{\pi_1} X_0 = \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_1}, TR_{m_1}) \xrightarrow{f_1} X_1 = \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_1}, T^{\otimes k_1}R_{m_1}) \xrightarrow{f_2 \circ (\pi_2^\circledast)^{\otimes r_2}} X_2 \xrightarrow{f_3, \dots, f_M} X_M\) (Strukturkaskade).

§7.3.3: Finite-Depth Cascade Norm Bound Theorem & Induction Proof

STRATUM B: SCHOLIUM 7.18, THEOREM 7.19 & COMPLETE INDUCTION PROOF | FORMALIZATION STAGE S₂ (LEAN 4)

Scholium 7.18 & Theorem 7.19 (Finite-Depth Layered Field Cascade Norm Estimate): Let \((X_\gamma)_{\gamma=0}^M\) be Banach spaces of bounded tensor sections and \(f_\gamma \colon X_{\gamma-1}^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi r_\gamma} \to X_\gamma\) be bounded multilinear operators with \(\|f_\gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le C_\gamma < \infty\) (\(\gamma = 1, \dots, M\)). For \(A_\gamma \coloneqq f_\gamma(A_{\gamma-1}, \dots, A_{\gamma-1})\), every stage \(1 \le \gamma \le M\) satisfies the monomial power bound: \[ \boxed{\|A_\gamma\|_{C_b^0} \;\le\; \Gamma_\gamma \, \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_\gamma}, \qquad D_\gamma \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^\gamma r_j, \qquad \Gamma_\gamma \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^\gamma C_j^{\prod_{\ell=j+1}^\gamma r_\ell}} \] with \(\Gamma_1 = C_1\). (Safety mechanism preventing recursive metric fields from blowing up into unphysical singularities.)

Proof of Theorem 7.19 (Mathematical Induction on Cascade Depth \(\gamma \ge 1\)): 1. Base Case (\(\gamma = 1\)): \(A_1 = f_1(A_0, \dots, A_0) \implies \|A_1\|_{C_b^0} \le \|f_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}\prod_{i=1}^{r_1}\|A_0\|_{C_b^0} \le C_1 \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{r_1}\). Since \(D_1 = r_1\) and \(\Gamma_1 = C_1^{\prod_{\ell=2}^1 r_\ell} = C_1^1 = C_1\), the base case holds. 2. Inductive Step (\(\gamma - 1 \to \gamma\)): Assume \(\|A_{\gamma-1}\|_{C_b^0} \le \Gamma_{\gamma-1}\|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_{\gamma-1}}\). Evaluating \(A_\gamma = f_\gamma(A_{\gamma-1}, \dots, A_{\gamma-1})\): \[ \|A_\gamma\|_{C_b^0} \le C_\gamma \|A_{\gamma-1}\|_{C_b^0}^{r_\gamma} \le C_\gamma \left(\Gamma_{\gamma-1}\|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_{\gamma-1}}\right)^{r_\gamma} = \left(C_\gamma \Gamma_{\gamma-1}^{r_\gamma}\right) \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{r_\gamma D_{\gamma-1}} \] 3. Exponent & Constant Aggregation: \(r_\gamma D_{\gamma-1} = \prod_{j=1}^\gamma r_j = D_\gamma\), and \(C_\gamma \Gamma_{\gamma-1}^{r_\gamma} = C_\gamma \prod_{j=1}^{\gamma-1} C_j^{(\prod_{\ell=j+1}^{\gamma-1} r_\ell)r_\gamma} = \prod_{j=1}^\gamma C_j^{\prod_{\ell=j+1}^\gamma r_\ell} = \Gamma_\gamma\). \(\blacksquare\)

theorem cascade_inductive_step (A_prev A_next C_g Γ_prev A0 : ℝ) (r_g D_prev : ℕ)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C_g) (hA : 0 ≤ A_prev) (h_ind : A_prev ≤ Γ_prev * A0 ^ D_prev)
    (h_op : A_next ≤ C_g * A_prev ^ r_g) :
    A_next ≤ (C_g * Γ_prev ^ r_g) * A0 ^ (D_prev * r_g) := by
  calc A_next ≤ C_g * (Γ_prev * A0 ^ D_prev) ^ r_g :=
         le_trans h_op (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (pow_le_pow_left hA h_ind r_g) hC)
       _ = (C_g * Γ_prev ^ r_g) * A0 ^ (D_prev * r_g) := by ring

§8.1.2: Separation der Variablen, Asymmetries & Ganzläufigkeit

STRATUM D: VARIABLE SEPARATION, FUNKTIONALE ASYMMETRIEN & GANZLÄUFIGE ÄONDYNEN (SM, P. 132)

Separation der Variablen (Variable Separation, SM p. 132): When a functional Synkolator \(\funktionaloperator\) acts upon multiple coordinates \((x_1, \dots, x_m)\), the generated Synkolationsfeld can be analytically decomposed into an algebraic or functional product of independent single-variable factors: \[ f(x_1, \dots, x_m) \;=\; \prod_{l=1}^m \phi_l(x_l) \] * Analytical Importance: Factors complex multi-dimensional field phenomena into isolated 1D functional channels, enabling independent examination of each coordinate’s contribution.

Funktionale Asymmetrien & Ganzläufige Äondynen (SM, p. 132): 1. Funktionale Asymmetrien (Functional Asymmetries): In physical systems, coordinates rarely enter generative laws symmetrically—spatial coordinates, temporal duration, and electrostatic charge play structurally distinct roles. Variable separation exposes these anisotropic weightings within the Synkolator kernel. 2. Ganzläufige Äondyne (Path-Dependent Synkolator Evolution): The functional Synkolator \(\funktionaloperator\) is not held fixed, but is itself continuously parameterized over an auxiliary Synkolationstensorium \(R_N\): \[ \funktionaloperator \;\equiv\; \funktionaloperator(t'), \qquad t' \in R_{m_s} \coloneqq M'_U \] Endows the quantified system with adaptive, context-sensitive learning capabilities as generative rules evolve smoothly across time or boundary conditions.

§8.1.4 & §8.2: Algebraic Constraints & Grothendieck Nuclearity

STRATUM D/A: ALGEBRAIC CONSTRAINTS (SM, P. 133) & GROTHENDIECK NUCLEARITY SCHOLIUM 8.2

§8.1.4 Three Algebraic Constraints on \(R_n\) (SM, p. 133): Because coordinates \(x_l\) spanning \(R_n\) are continua derived from algebraic number fields (\(\zahlenkoerper\)), all quantitative operations obey three strict constraints: 1. Fehlstelle 0 and Einheit E: Every coordinate continuum \(x_l\) intrinsically contains the additive identity (\(0\), origin state or Fehlstelle) and multiplicative identity (\(E \equiv 1\), unit scaling element): \[ \{0, 1\} \subset x_l \quad \forall l \in \{1, \dots, n\} \] 2. Reduzierbarkeit homometraler Formen: Synkolation operations with repeated parameter inputs (homometral sampling with replacement) reduce algebraically to distinct inputs of lower effective arity \(A < m\). 3. 3-Class Corporate Collapse: Functional operations over number fields cannot be composed without coupling, collapsing the \(15\) general corporate classes to \(3\) operative types.

Scholium 8.2 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Cornered Manifolds & Nuclearity): Why formalize \(R_n\) as a smooth manifold with corners \(\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\) and evaluate kernels in the nuclear Fréchet space \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)\)? * Physical Positivity & Origin Boundary: Fundamental physical magnitudes (mass, radial distance, absolute temperature, energy density) satisfy \(0 \le x_i < \infty\), with Fehlstelle \(\mathbf{0} \in \mathcal{M}_n\) and boundary faces \(\partial_i \mathcal{M}_n = \{x_i = 0\}\). * Grothendieck’s Dual Legacy (Zalamea 2012; Marquis 2009): Alexander Grothendieck created both topos theory (Ch. 1) and nuclear locally convex spaces (1955). Whereas infinite-dimensional Banach spaces are never nuclear (\(\otpi \ne \oteps\)), \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)\) is strictly nuclear: \[ \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_{m_1} \times \mathcal{M}_{m_2}) \;\cong\; \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_{m_1}) \otpi \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_{m_2}) \;\cong\; \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_{m_1}) \oteps \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_{m_2}) \] embedding densely into \(C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n)\) as the exact engine for Separation der Variablen.

Intrinsic Arithmetic Anchors (\(\{0, 1\} \subset x_l\), SM p. 133):
In qualitative categories (Teil A), carriers lack canonical zero or unit elements. In \(\Ctxquant\), every coordinate continuum carries the origin basepoint \(\mathbf{0}\) (Fehlstelle 0, where syndrome fields vanish or anchor) and unit scale \(E \equiv 1_{\mathbb{K}}\), ensuring arithmetic normalization and scaling across all \(n\) dimensions.
Smooth Manifolds with Corners \(\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\):
The boundary \(\partial \mathcal{M}_n = \bigcup_{i=1}^n \partial_i \mathcal{M}_n\) consists of \(n\) coordinate hyperplanes \(\partial_i \mathcal{M}_n = \{x \in \mathcal{M}_n \mid x_i = 0\}\) intersecting at the origin corner \(\mathbf{0} = (0,\dots,0)\). Smoothness up to all boundary faces requires one-sided derivatives of all orders to extend continuously to \(x_i \to 0^+\).
Zalamea (2012) & Marquis (2009) Synthesis:
Grothendieck’s 1955 Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires proves that in nuclear Fréchet spaces, the projective tensor completion \(\otpi\) and injective tensor completion \(\oteps\) coincide canonically. This eliminates cross-norm ambiguity when factoring multi-variable physical fields.
Why Banach Spaces Alone Cannot Factor Smooth Kernels:
By the Dvoretzky–Rogers / Grothendieck theorem, a normed space is nuclear if and only if it is finite-dimensional! Working in the nuclear Fréchet subalgebra \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n) \hookrightarrow C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n)\) gives an exact tensor isomorphism while remaining compatible with our bounded Banach sections.

§8.2.1: Cornered Parameter Manifolds \(\Manparam\) & Base Envelope

STRATUM A: CATEGORY OF PARAMETER MANIFOLDS WITH CORNERS (DEF. 8.3) & BASE RING ENVELOPE (DEF. 8.4)

Definition 8.3: Category of Parameter Manifolds with Corners \(\Manparam\) The category \(\Manparam\) consists of: 1. Objects: Smooth \(n\)-dimensional manifolds with corners \(\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\), equipped with the subspace topology and smooth structure up to all boundary faces. 2. Morphisms: Smooth proper contractions \(h \colon \mathcal{M}_m \to \mathcal{M}_n\) preserving the origin basepoint: \(h(\mathbf{0}) = \mathbf{0}\). 3. Nuclear Fréchet Algebra of Rapidly Decreasing Sections: For \(\mathcal{M}_n \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Manparam)\), \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)\) is the Schwartz space of smooth functions on \((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\) whose partial derivatives extend continuously to the boundary faces and decay rapidly at infinity, equipped with the countable family of seminorms: \[ \|f\|_{\alpha, \beta} \;\coloneqq\; \sup_{x \in \mathcal{M}_n} \left| x^\alpha \partial^\beta f(x) \right| < \infty \quad \forall \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}_0^n \] \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)\) is a nuclear Fréchet algebra that embeds continuously into the unital Fréchet algebra \(C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n)\) of smooth functions with bounded derivatives.

Definition 8.4: The Algebraic Base Ring Envelope \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{M}_n)\) Let \(\mathbb{K} \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Coeff)\). The Unital Algebraic Base Envelope of \(\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\) is the unitization topological \(\mathbb{K}\)-algebra: \[ \mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{M}_n) \;\coloneqq\; \mathbb{K} \cdot 1_{\mathcal{A}} \;\oplus\; \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n, \mathbb{K}) \;\subset\; C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n, \mathbb{K}) \] containing the nuclear ideal \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n, \mathbb{K}) \cong \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n) \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{K}\) together with the multiplicative identity section \(1_{\mathcal{A}} \colon x \mapsto 1_{\mathbb{K}}\) (Einheit E) and the additive identity section \(0_{\mathcal{A}} \colon x \mapsto 0_{\mathbb{K}}\) (as well as the geometric origin basepoint \(\mathbf{0} \in \mathcal{M}_n\), Fehlstelle 0).

§8.2.2: Exterior Differential \(\dtilde\), Poincaré Integral \(\Izero\) & Carnap 8.1

STRATUM A: EXTERIOR DIFFERENTIAL & POINCARÉ HOMOTOPY INTEGRAL (DEF. 8.5) & CARNAP SCHOLIUM 8.1

Definition 8.5: Exterior Differential & Poincaré Homotopy Integral on Corners Let \(\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\) and \(C_{\mathbf{0}}^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n) \coloneqq \{f \in C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n) \mid f(\mathbf{0}) = 0\}\). 1. Whitney Closed Bounded 1-Forms \(\Omega_{\mathrm{closed},b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n)\): Smooth 1-forms \(\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n \omega_i(x)\,dx^i\) on \((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\) (smooth up to the boundary in the sense of Whitney) satisfying \(d\omega = 0\). 2. Infinitesimal Differential Functor \(\dtilde \colon C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n) \to \Omega_{\mathrm{closed},b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n)\): \[ \dtilde f \;\coloneqq\; df \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\parttilde_i| f\right) dx^i \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^i} dx^i \tag{SM-30} \] where \(\parttilde_i| f(x) \coloneqq \lim_{\Delta x^i \to 0^+} \frac{f(x + \Delta x^i e_i) - f(x)}{\Delta x^i}\). 3. Poincaré Homotopy Integral Functor \(\Izero \colon \Omega_{\mathrm{closed},b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n) \to C^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n)\): Integrates \(\omega\) along the radial ray \(\gamma_x(t) = tx\) (\(t \in [0,1]\)) from \(\mathbf{0} \in \mathcal{M}_n\): \[ \left(\Izero\,\omega\right)(x) \;\coloneqq\; \int_0^1 \sum_{i=1}^n x^i \omega_i(tx)\,dt \] satisfying path-independence and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus on the star-shaped octant \(\mathcal{M}_n\) for any smooth path \(\gamma \colon [a,b] \to \mathcal{M}_n\): \[ \dtilde\left(\Izero\,\omega\right) = \omega, \qquad \Izero(\dtilde f)(x) = f(x) - f(\mathbf{0}), \qquad \mathrm{I}_a^b(\dtilde f) = f(\gamma(b)) - f(\gamma(a)) \tag{SM-33} \]

Carnap 8.1: Synthetic Infinitesimals (Kock–Lawvere) vs. Discrete Metronics In Synthetic Differential Geometry (SDG; Kock 1981, Lawvere 1979), differentiation is formalized algebraically inside a smooth topos via square-zero infinitesimals \(D \coloneqq \llbracket d \in R \mid d^2 = 0 \rrbracket \subset R\) with \(\forall d \in D,\; f(x+d) = f(x) + f'(x)d\). \[ \boxed{\text{SDG provides an internal infinitesimal calculus; DEC provides a discrete cochain calculus.}} \] These are distinct mathematical architectures and modeling strata (\(\mathbf{A}\) and \(\mathbf{C}\)); constructing a formal or functorial bridge is a separate reconstruction problem, not a deductive identity.

§8.3.1: Corner Smoothness & Seeley Extension Operator (Thm. 8.6)

STRATUM B: WHY NAIVE APPROACHES FAIL II, SEELEY EXTENSION ON CORNERS (THM. 8.6 PART 1 & FIG. 8.2)

Why Naive Approaches Fail II: Boundary Smoothness at a Corner * A zero extension across \(x=0\) preserves smoothness only when every boundary derivative vanishes; for \(e^{-x}\) on \(x \ge 0\), \(f(0^+) = 1 \ne 0\), so zero extension is discontinuous. * Even reflection \(e^{-|x|}\) is continuous, but has a jump in its first derivative at \(x=0\) (\(f'(0^+) = -1 \ne f'(0^-) = +1\)), destroying Schwartz seminorms \(\|f\|_{\alpha,\beta}\). * Resolution: Robert Seeley’s (1964) extension operator constructs a moment-matched linear combination of dyadically rescaled reflections across each boundary hyperplane, preserving all Schwartz seminorms on corners!

Theorem 8.6 (Part 1): Multidimensional Seeley Extension on Corners (Fig. 8.2) Let \(\mathcal{M}_n \coloneqq (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n\) (with \(R_n(\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathbb{R}^{2n}\) in real Cartesian coordinates). Following Seeley (1964), let \(\chi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) satisfy \(\chi(t)=1\) for \(|t|\le 1\) and \(\chi(t)=0\) for \(|t|\ge 2\), and let \((a_k)_{k=0}^\infty\) be a rapidly decreasing sequence (\(\sum_{k=0}^\infty |a_k| 2^{km} < \infty\) \(\forall m \in \mathbb{N}_0\)) satisfying the Vandermonde moment identities: \[ \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k (-2^k)^m \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall m \in \mathbb{N}_0 \] Then the coordinatewise extension \(\mathcal{E}_{x_i} f(x_i) \coloneqq \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k \chi(-2^k x_i) f(-2^k x_i)\) (\(x_i < 0\)) and its tensor product \(\mathcal{E}^{(n)} \coloneqq \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \mathcal{E}_{x_i} \colon \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n) \to \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)\) define a continuous linear right-inverse to restriction \(\mathcal{R}_+ \colon \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n) \twoheadrightarrow \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n)\): \[ \mathcal{R}_+ \circ \mathcal{E}^{(n)} \;=\; \operatorname{id}_{\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)}, \qquad P \coloneqq \mathcal{E}^{(n)} \circ \mathcal{R}_+ \;=\; P^2 \]

STRATUM B: GROTHENDIECK NUCLEARITY ON CORNERS (THM. 8.6 PARTS 2–4, FIG. 8.1), FULL PROOF & TOY EXAMPLE

Theorem 8.6 (Parts 2–4): Nuclearity Inheritance & Tensor Expansion (Fig. 8.1) * Nuclearity Inheritance: Because \(\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n)\) is isomorphic via \(\mathcal{E}^{(n)}\) to the closed complemented subspace \(\operatorname{Im}(\mathcal{E}^{(n)} \circ \mathcal{R}_+) \subset \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)\), it inherits nuclearity from \(\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)\) (Grothendieck 1955; Ryan 2002): \[ \mathscr{S}\!\left((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m\right) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{l=1}^{m,\pi} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{l=1}^{m,\varepsilon} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}) \] * Projective Tensor Expansion: Every rapid-decay synkolation kernel \(f \in \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)\) admits an absolutely convergent projective tensor expansion into 1D factors with bounded \(\{\phi_j^{(l)}\} \subset \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})\): \[ f(x_1, \dots, x_m) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^\infty \lambda_j \, \phi_j^{(1)}(x_1) \otimes \dots \otimes \phi_j^{(m)}(x_m), \qquad \sum_{j=1}^\infty |\lambda_j| < \infty \] * Claim Ceiling (\(c_{\mathrm{NUCL}}\)): Grothendieck nuclearity guarantees an absolutely convergent series of separated tensor products in \(\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)\); finite-rank (single-product) ODE separability holds iff the kernel has tensor rank \(1\).

Proof of Theorem 8.6 & Toy Example (\(f(x_1,x_2) = e^{-(x_1+x_2)}\cos(x_1 x_2)\)): 1. Step 1 (Derivative Matching): Differentiating \(\mathcal{E}_{x_i} f\) term-by-term for \(x_i < 0\) via \(\sum |a_k| 2^{km} < \infty\) yields \(\lim_{x_i \to 0^-} \partial_{x_i}^m(\mathcal{E}_{x_i}f) = (\sum a_k(-2^k)^m)\partial_{x_i}^m f(0^+) = \partial_{x_i}^m f(0^+)\), preserving all Schwartz seminorms \(\|\cdot\|_{\alpha,\beta}\). 2. Step 2 (Idempotent Retract): \(P = \mathcal{E}^{(n)} \circ \mathcal{R}_+\) satisfies \(P^2 = P\), identifying \(\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)\) with the closed subspace \(\operatorname{Im}(P) \subset \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)\). 3. Step 3 (Nuclear Permanence): Closed subspaces of nuclear Fréchet spaces are nuclear (Grothendieck 1955), yielding the series expansion. \(\blacksquare\) * Toy Example (Remark): \(f(x_1,x_2) = e^{-(x_1+x_2)}\cos(x_1 x_2) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^k}{(2k)!}(x_1^{2k}e^{-x_1})\otimes(x_2^{2k}e^{-x_2})\) with \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty |\lambda_k| = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(2k)!} = \cosh(1) \approx 1.543 < \infty\).

§8.3.2: Homometral Reducibility & Polarization on \(\Sym^m(V)\)

STRATUM B: POLARIZATION SCHOLIUM 8.7, HOMOMETRAL REDUCIBILITY THEOREM 8.8, PROOF & CUBIC TOY EXAMPLE

Scholium 8.7 (Polarization and Effective Arity): Polarization reconstructs the multilinear form hidden by repeated inputs. Consequently, homometral sampling can be reduced to the genuinely distinct channels that carry new information, clarifying why effective arity may be smaller than nominal arity.

Theorem 8.8: Homometral Reduction in Symmetric Polynomial Envelopes Let \(V\) be an \(n\)-dimensional real vector space with basis \(\{e_1, \dots, e_n\}\) and \(\Sym^m(V)\) the \(m\)-th symmetric tensor power. 1. Polarization Identity: Every element \(v^m \in \Sym^m(V)\) generated by repeated (homometral) evaluation of \(v = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i e_i\) decomposes uniquely into a linear combination of distinct (heterometral) symmetrized tensor products: \[ v^m \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^m \sum_{1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n} c_{i_1 \dots i_k} \left( e_{i_1} \odot \dots \odot e_{i_k} \right) \] 2. Arity Reduction: For any polynomial operadic functional \(F \in \Oquant\) of nominal arity \(m\) evaluated on \(k < m\) distinct coordinates with multiplicities \((a_1, \dots, a_k)\) (\(\sum a_j = m\)), there exists a unique reduced operator \(F_{\mathrm{red}} \in \Oquant(k; 1)\) of strict arity \(k\) such that: \[ F(\underbrace{x_1, \dots, x_1}_{a_1}, \dots, \underbrace{x_k, \dots, x_k}_{a_k}) \;=\; F_{\mathrm{red}}(x_1, \dots, x_k) \]

Proof of Theorem 8.8 & Cubic Toy Example (\(m=3, k=2\)): * Proof: By the classical multilinear polarization identity, \(P(v) = v^m\) is uniquely reconstructed from \(m\) distinct slots via: \[ \Pol(v_1, \dots, v_m) \;=\; \frac{1}{2^m m!} \sum_{\epsilon \in \{-1, 1\}^m} \left(\prod_{i=1}^m \epsilon_i\right) \left( \sum_{j=1}^m \epsilon_j v_j \right)^m \] When the input tuple contains only \(k < m\) distinct variables, grouping identical slots collapses the summation domain onto a \(k\)-ary operator \(F_{\mathrm{red}} \colon V^{\otimes k} \to W\) of strict effective arity \(k < m\). \(\blacksquare\) * Cubic Toy Example: A tertiary Synkolator (\(m=3\)) evaluating \(F(x_1, x_1, x_2) = x_1^2 x_2\) (multiplicities \(a_1=2, a_2=1\)) reduces to \(F_{\mathrm{red}}(u,v) \coloneqq u^2 v \in \Oquant(2;1)\) of strict binary arity \(k = 2 < 3\) (SM, p. 133).

Theorem 8.9: Algebraic Collapse of Corporate Classes in \(\Ctxquant\) Let \(\mathcal{S}_a, \mathcal{S}_b \in \Synquant\) be quantitative Syntrix algebras over parameter manifolds \(R_{n_a}, R_{n_b}\) valued in a coefficient field \(\mathbb{K} \in \Coeff\). 1. Identification of Carrier & Functional Tiers: Because every quantitative Synkolator \(f \in \Oquant\) is a \(\mathbb{K}\)-valued functional operator evaluated directly on the coordinates of \(R_n\) via the ring operations of \(\mathbb{K}\), the synkolative rule selection (\(K_s, C_s\)) cannot vary independently of the metrophoric carrier selection (\(K_m, C_m\)): an uncoupled carrier coproduct forces block-diagonal functional composition, while carrier coordinate coupling forces functional cross-modulation. 2. 15-to-3 Class Reduction: Restricting the \(2 \times 2\) corporate rule matrix \(\left\{\begin{smallmatrix} K_s & C_s \\ K_m & C_m \end{smallmatrix}\right\}\) to synchronized column selections (\(K \coloneqq \{K_m, K_s\}\) and \(C \coloneqq \{C_m, C_s\}\)) collapses the \(2^4 - 1 = 15\) general corporate classes (Ch. 3) to the \(2^2 - 1 = \mathbf{3}\) non-empty subsets of \(\{K, C\}\) (SM, pp. 133–135): \[ \operatorname{Op}_{\mathrm{quant}} \;=\; \Big\{\; \mathbf{Kor}_{\{K\}} \ (\text{Pure Coupled}), \;\; \mathbf{Kor}_{\{C\}} \ (\text{Pure Parallel}), \;\; \mathbf{Kor}_{\{K, C\}} \ (\text{Partial Coupling + Composition}) \;\Big\} \]

Proof of Theorem 8.9: In the qualitative category \(\mathbf{Syn}\) (Ch. 3), \(\{K_m, C_m\}\) and \(\{K_s, C_s\}\) can be chosen independently (\(2^4 - 1 = 15\) subsets). In \(\Synquant\), every syndrome section \(A_\gamma \in \Gamma_b^0(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m)\) is a function of the base parameter manifold \(R_m\). If \(R_{m_a}, R_{m_b}\) share \(\lambda > 0\) coupled coordinates in the pushout \(R_{m_a} \boxplus_\phi R_{m_b}\), evaluating functional operators across shared coordinates automatically induces synkolative coupling \(K_s\); on uncoupled summands (\(\lambda = 0\)), operators act in parallel (\(C_s\)). Thus the active corporate rule is determined by a non-empty subset of \(\{K, C\}\), yielding \(2^2 - 1 = 3\) classes. \(\blacksquare\)

Remark (Heim’s Mixed-Variant Covariant Derivative & Transposition Argument, SM pp. 159–160): For a tensor with \(\mu\) covariant and \(m-\mu\) contravariant indices: \[ A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu,k}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m} = \frac{\partial A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m}}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} - \sum_{\lambda=1}^{\mu}\begin{Bmatrix}s\\i_\lambda,k\end{Bmatrix}A_{i_1\cdots s\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m} + \sum_{\lambda=\mu+1}^{m}\begin{Bmatrix}i_\lambda\\s\;k\end{Bmatrix}A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{s}\cdots\underline{i}_m} \] For a parallel-transported covariant vector, subtracting its index-transposed form yields: \[ \frac{\partial A_i}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} - \frac{\partial A_k}{\partial x^{\underline{i}}} = A_s\left(\begin{Bmatrix}s\\i\;k\end{Bmatrix} - \begin{Bmatrix}s\\k\;i\end{Bmatrix}\right) \] Epistemic Caution: This identity contracts the skew connection with \(A_s\); a nonzero skew connection requires an explicit nonvanishing-curl and nondegeneracy premise.
