§9.3.1: Palatini Cross-Metric Connection Decomposition (Theorem 9.6, SM-53)

STRATUM B: DERIVED MATHEMATICAL THEOREMS — CROSS-METRIC CONNECTION & KOPPELUNGSTENSOR Q (THM. 9.6, SM EQ. 53)

Theorem 9.6 (Palatini Cross-Metric Connection Decomposition Theorem, SM Eq. 53): Let \(\{g_{(\gamma)}\}_{\gamma=1}^\omega \subset \operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})\) be \(\omega\) smooth non-Hermitian partial metrics on \(\mathcal{M}\), and \(g \coloneqq \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega g_{(\gamma)}\) their composite sum metric with right-inverse \(g^{is}\) (\(g_{sa}g^{ak} = \delta_s^k\)). Let \([s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}(\partial_k g_{(\gamma)sl} + \partial_l g_{(\gamma)ks} - \partial_s g_{(\gamma)kl})\). 1. Exact Algebraic Decomposition (SM Eq. 53): The composite second-kind Christoffel symbols \(\Gamma_{kl}^i = \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}i\\kl\end{smallmatrix}\right\} \coloneqq g^{is}[s\,k\,l]\) decompose identically as: \[ \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{smallmatrix} \right\} \;=\; \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega \left( \begin{Bmatrix} i \\ k \; l \end{Bmatrix}^{(\mu)}_{(\gamma)} + \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \begin{Bmatrix} m \\ k \; l \end{Bmatrix}^{(\mu)}_{(\gamma)} \right) \tag{SM-53} \] where \(\begin{Bmatrix}i\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} \coloneqq g_{(\mu)}^{\dagger,is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)}\) is the cross-metric connection (Korrelationstensor) and the Koppelungstensor is the exact algebraic difference tensor: \[ \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \;\coloneqq\; g^{is} g_{(\mu)sm} - \frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i \] 2. Decoupling Criterion: \(\mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \equiv 0 \iff g_{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\omega}g\;\;\forall \mu \in \{1,\dots,\omega\}\) (homothety alignment). Anisotropy or misalignment forces \(\mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)} \ne \mathbf{0}\), generating non-linear cross-metric interactions.

Proof of Theorem 9.6 (Exact 3-Step Algebraic Factorization): 1. Linearity of 1st-kind symbols: \([s\,k\,l] = \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega [s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} \implies \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}i\\kl\end{smallmatrix}\right\} = \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega g^{is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)}\). 2. Resolution of identity: Using \(\delta_a^s = g_{(\mu)am}g_{(\mu)}^{\dagger,ms}\), insert \(\sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \delta_a^s\): \[ g^{is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} = \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega (g^{ia}g_{(\mu)am})\begin{Bmatrix}m\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} = \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \left(\frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i + \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i\right)\begin{Bmatrix}m\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} \] 3. Homothety limit: If \(g_{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\omega}g\), then \(g^{ia}g_{(\mu)am} = \frac{1}{\omega}g^{ia}g_{am} = \frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i \implies \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \equiv 0\). \(\blacksquare\)

§9.3.1b: Contortion Tensor \(\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i\), Curvature Splitting & Ricci Density Curl

STRATUM B: ALGEBRAIC CONTORTION TENSOR (DEF. 9.13), CURVATURE SPLITTING & RICCI VOLUME-DENSITY CURL (LEMMA 9.7, SM-51)

Definition 9.13 (Algebraic Contortion Tensor in Non-Hermitian Palatini Gravity): Let \(T_{kl}^i \coloneqq \Gamma_{[kl]}^i = \frac{1}{2}(\Gamma_{kl}^i - \Gamma_{lk}^i)\) be the metric torsion tensor of the non-Hermitian connection. The Contortion Tensor \(\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i\) is the unique linear tensor satisfying: \[ \Gamma_{kl}^i = \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{smallmatrix} \right\}_{{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+} + \mathbf{K}_{kl}^i, \qquad K_{ikl} \coloneqq g_{is} \mathbf{K}_{kl}^s = \frac{1}{2}\left( T_{ikl} + T_{lik} - T_{kli} \right) \] where \(T_{ikl} \coloneqq g_{is}T_{kl}^s\). If the skew-symmetric metric sector vanishes (\({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- \equiv \mathbf{0} \implies T_{kl}^i \equiv 0\)), then \(K_{ikl} \equiv 0\), recovering the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection.

Remark (Curvature Decomposition Under a Contortion \(\Gamma = \Gamma^{(+)} + \mathbf{K}\)): With \(R^i{}_{klm} = \partial_l\Gamma^i_{km} - \partial_m\Gamma^i_{kl} + \Gamma^i_{sl}\Gamma^s_{km} - \Gamma^i_{sm}\Gamma^s_{kl}\), direct expansion yields the exact curvature splitting: \[ R^i{}_{klm}(\Gamma) = R^{(+)i}{}_{klm} + \nabla^{(+)}_l\mathbf{K}^i{}_{km} - \nabla^{(+)}_m\mathbf{K}^i{}_{kl} + \mathbf{K}^i{}_{sl}\mathbf{K}^s{}_{km} - \mathbf{K}^i{}_{sm}\mathbf{K}^s{}_{kl} \] Epistemic Note: This is an exact differential-geometric curvature decomposition; an Einstein–Maxwell physical interpretation requires additional field equations and a justified source ansatz.

Lemma 9.7 (Determinant Curl Term in the Ricci Splitting, SM Eq. 51, p. 179): Let \(w \coloneqq \sqrt{|\det g|}\) denote the metric volume density and \(\llcorner_l w\) Heim’s covariant volume-density derivative. The common \(2\times 2\) operator-determinant term in the symmetric and skew Ricci components expands as a curl-like contribution: \[ \frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} \partial_l & \partial_k \\ \frac{1}{w}\llcorner_l & \frac{1}{w}\llcorner_k \end{vmatrix} w = \frac{1}{2}\left[ \partial_l\!\left(\frac{1}{w}\llcorner_k w\right) - \partial_k\!\left(\frac{1}{w}\llcorner_l w\right) \right] \tag{SM-51} \]

STRATUM B & CARNAP SCHOLIUM 9.1: PALATINI COMPATIBILITY, EINSTEIN CONSERVATION (SM-49) & DAMOUR–DESER–MCCARTHY NO-GO

Why Naive Approaches Fail III: Ricci Flow’s Diffeomorphism Degeneracy The unmodified Ricci-flow operator is not strongly parabolic: infinitesimal coordinate changes lie in the kernel of its principal symbol. Introducing the DeTurck vector field relative to background metric \(\bar{g}\): \[ V^k = g^{pq}\bigl(\Gamma_{pq}^k(g) - \Gamma_{pq}^k(\bar{g})\bigr) \] adds \(\mathcal{L}_V g = \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i\), removing the principal-symbol degeneracy so \(\sigma_\xi(\mathcal{T}(g))h_{ij} = \|\xi\|_g^2 h_{ij}\) becomes strictly elliptic and strongly parabolic.

Theorem 9.14 (Palatini Connection Uniqueness & Sobolev Fixed-Point Convergence): Let \(\mathcal{M}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and fix \(\bar{g} \in \operatorname{Met}^+(\mathcal{M})\). 1. Unique Palatini Resolution: Under the Einstein–Kaufman transposition constraint and \({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}^{(2)} \equiv 0\), Palatini variation uniquely fixes \(\Gamma_{kl}^i\) in terms of \({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\) and \(\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i\) (Thm. 9.8). 2. DeTurck-Modified Cascade Operator: Let \(\mathcal{T}(g)_{ij} \coloneqq -2R_{ij}(g) + \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i\). For Sobolev index \(s > \frac{n}{2} + 2\), the heat-regularized cascade operator: \[ \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}} \;\coloneqq\; e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{\bar{g}} + c_0 I)} \circ \mathcal{T} \;\colon\; H^s(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2 T^*\mathcal{M}) \longrightarrow H^s(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2 T^*\mathcal{M}) \] is a strict Banach contraction on \(\mathbf{B}_{H^s}(\bar{g}, \delta)\) for \(\tau_M \ge \tau_M^*\): \[ \|\mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g_1) - \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g_2)\|_{H^s} \;\le\; k_M \|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s}, \qquad k_M \coloneqq C_{\text{heat}}C_{\text{geom}}(\bar{g},\delta)\frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} < 1 \] 3. Unique Smooth Apex Metric: By the Banach Fixed-Point Theorem and elliptic regularity bootstrapping, \(g^{(m+1)} = \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g^{(m)})\) converges geometrically in \(H^s\) to a unique \({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in \bigcap_{k=s}^\infty H^k(\mathcal{M}) = C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\). \(\blacksquare\)

Theorem 9.15 (Unsatisfiability of Literal Formula 61) & Proof: Heim’s SM Eq. 61 specifies \(L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1}\) (\(1 \le \omega_1 < n\)), \(L_\alpha = \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}\), and apex order \(\omega_M = n/2\). Under the apex condition \(L_M = 1\), the literal cascade equalities are inconsistent for every \(n \ge 2\). * Proof: Since \(\binom{m}{k} \ge m\) for \(1 \le k < m\), we have \(L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1} \ge n\) and \(L_{M-1} \ge L_1 \ge n\). But \(L_M = \binom{L_{M-1}}{\omega_M} = 1\) forces \(\omega_M = L_{M-1} \ge n\), contradicting \(\omega_M = n/2\) for \(n \ge 2\). \(\blacksquare\)

  • The Metron (\(\tau > 0\)): Indivisible quantum of geometric area (\(\tau = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\ell_P^2 \approx 1.13115 \times 10^{-70}\,\text{m}^2\)), integer Metronenziffer \(N_i \in \mathbb{Z}\), directional selector \(\chi_i\), and Metronenfunktionen \(\phi(n)\) on the Metronische Gitter (\(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n\)). Eliminating \(\Delta x \to 0\) removes UV infinities identically.

§10.1.2: Metrondifferentiale (\(F\phi \equiv \nabla\phi\)) & Extremwerttheorie

STRATUM D: FIRST & HIGHER METRONDIFFERENTIALS, LEIBNIZ PRODUCT & DISCRETE EXTREMA (SM, PP. 211–218, EQS. 67–68b)

First and Higher Metrondifferentials (SM Eqs. 67–68, pp. 213–215): * Because \(\Delta x \to 0\) is physically forbidden, Heim replaces differential quotients with the backward Metrondifferential (\(F\phi \equiv \nabla\phi\)): \[ F\phi(n) \equiv \nabla\phi(n) \coloneqq \phi(n) - \phi(n-1) \tag{SM-67} \] measuring change realized upon reaching state \(n\) from its immediate historical predecessor \(n-1\) (preserving causal arrow determinism). * Iterating \(F\) yields the \(k\)-th binomial expansion: \[ F^k\phi(n) = \sum_{\gamma=0}^k (-1)^\gamma \binom{k}{\gamma} \phi(n - \gamma) \tag{SM-68} \]

Discrete Product Cross-Term (SM-68a) & Metronische Extremwerttheorie (SM-68b): * Product Difference (SM-68a, p. 216): Features a non-linear discreteness signature \(-Fu(n)Fv(n)\) scaling as \((\Delta x)^2 \to 0\) in the continuum limit: \[ F(u(n)v(n)) = u(n)Fv(n) + v(n-1)Fu(n) = u(n)Fv(n) + v(n)Fu(n) - Fu(n)Fv(n) \tag{SM-68a} \] * Discrete Extrema & Inflection Nodes (Wendepunkte, SM-68b, p. 217): Node \(n=e\) is a discrete extremum if \(F\phi(e) = 0\) (or changes sign): maximum if \(F^2\phi(e) < 0\), minimum if \(F^2\phi(e) > 0\), and inflection node \(w\) if: \[ \nabla^2\phi(w)\cdot\nabla^2\phi(w+1) < 0 \;\lor\; \big(\nabla^2\phi(w) = 0 \;\wedge\; \nabla^2\phi(w-1)\cdot\nabla^2\phi(w+1) < 0\big) \]

§10.1.3: Das Metronintegral (\(\mathcal{S}\phi\)) & Hauptsatz der Metronik

STRATUM D: INDEFINITE/DEFINITE METRONINTEGRAL, DOMAIN-SPLITTING & SUMMATION BY PARTS (SM, PP. 217–220, EQS. 67a–71)

The Metronintegral (\(S\phi \equiv \mathcal{S}\phi\), SM §8.1.3, pp. 217–220): 1. Indefinite Metronintegral (SM Eq. 70, p. 219): Primitive sequence \(\Phi(n)\) satisfying \(F\Phi(n) = \phi(n)\) with unit lattice step \(Fn = 1\): \[ \Phi(n) = \mathcal{S}\phi(n)\,Fn + C \iff \mathcal{S}\phi(n)\,Fn = \Phi(n) - C \tag{SM-70} \] Boundary-Index Forms (SM p. 219): \[ \mathcal{S}_a^n \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = \Phi(n)-\Phi(a-1), \quad \mathcal{S}_n^b \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = \Phi(b)-\Phi(n-1), \quad \mathcal{S}_{n+1}^b \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = \Phi(b)-\Phi(n) \] Varying the lower endpoint gives \(\nabla_n \mathcal{S}_{n+1}^b \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = -\nabla\Phi(n) = -\phi(n)\). 2. Definite Metronintegral (SM Eq. 67a, p. 214): Telescoping over \([n_1, n_2]\): \[ J(n_1, n_2) \coloneqq \sum_{n=n_1}^{n_2} \phi(n) \equiv \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2} \phi(n)\,\Delta n = \Phi(n_2) - \Phi(n_1 - 1) \tag{SM-67a} \]

Domain-Splitting Laws (SM Eq. 69, p. 218) & Summation by Parts (SM Eq. 71): \[ \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^\gamma \phi + \mathcal{S}_{\gamma+1}^{n_2} \phi = \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2} \phi, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_1+1}\phi = 0, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_1}\phi\,\Delta n = \Phi(n_1) \] \[ \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2}\phi + \mathcal{S}_{n_2}^{n_1}\phi = \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_1}\phi + \mathcal{S}_{n_2}^{n_2}\phi \tag{SM-69} \] * Discrete Summation by Parts (SM Eq. 71): Inverting the discrete product rule yields: \[ \mathcal{S}(u\nabla v)(n) \coloneqq \sum_{j=-\infty}^n u(j)\nabla v(j) = u(n)v(n) - \lim_{j\to-\infty} u(j)v(j) - \mathcal{S}\big((E^{-1}v)\nabla u\big)(n) \tag{SM-71} \]

§10.1.4: Partielle/Totale Differentiale, Transzendente Funktionen & Wronskian

STRATUM D: MULTI-VARIABLE DIFFERENCES, EULER HOMOGENEITY, TRANSCENDENTAL DIFFS & WRONSKIAN (SM, PP. 220–252, EQS. 73–82, THM. 10.2)

Multi-Variable Partial & Total Metrondifferentials (SM §8.1.4, pp. 220–231): 1. Partial Difference Operator (SM Eq. 73, p. 221) & Vertauschbarkeitssatz (SM Eq. 73a): \[ F_k\phi(n_1,\dots,n_L) \coloneqq \phi(n_1,\dots,n_k,\dots,n_L) - \phi(n_1,\dots,n_k-1,\dots,n_L), \qquad F_k F_l\phi = F_l F_k\phi \tag{SM-73/73a} \] 2. Total Metrondifferential (SM Eq. 74, p. 222): \[ \nabla_{\mathrm{tot}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^L \nabla_i\phi(\mathbf{n}), \qquad \nabla_i n_k = \delta_{ik} \tag{SM-74} \] 3. Nearest-Neighbor Lattice Theorem (SM Eq. 74a, p. 226): \[ L\phi(\mathbf{n}) - \nabla_{\mathrm{tot}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{i=1}^L \phi(\mathbf{n} - \mathbf{e}_i) \iff \frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=1}^L \phi(\mathbf{n}-\mathbf{e}_i) = \phi(\mathbf{n}) - \frac{1}{L}\nabla_{\mathrm{tot}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) \tag{SM-74a} \] 4. Discrete Euler Homogeneity Identity (SM Eq. 77, p. 231): For degree \(h\) and \(n=\pm 1\): \[ \pm \sum_{i=1}^L n_i\nabla_i\phi(\mathbf{n}) = (-1)^{h+1}\phi(\mathbf{n})\sum_{\gamma=0}^{h-1}\binom{h}{\gamma}(\mp 1)^\gamma \quad (n=\pm 1) \tag{SM-77} \] Upper signs (\(n=+1, x=-1\)) yield RHS \(\phi(\mathbf{n})\); lower signs (\(n=-1, x=+1\)) yield \((-1)^{h+1}(2^h-1)\phi(\mathbf{n})\).

4-Tab Inspector: Transcendental Differences (SM-81) & Discrete Wronskian (Thm. 10.2)

1. Logarithmic, Exponential & Euler Identities (SM Eqs. 81–81a, pp. 246–249): \[ \phi\,\nabla_\phi \ln\phi = \nabla\phi, \qquad \nabla_\phi e^\phi = e^\phi\,\nabla\phi \tag{SM-81} \] \[ e^{\mathrm{i}\phi} = \cos\phi + \mathrm{i}\sin\phi \tag{SM-81a} \]

2. Trigonometric & Hyperbolic Finite Differences (SM pp. 246–249): \[ \nabla_\phi\cos\phi = -\sin\phi\,\nabla\phi, \quad \nabla_\phi\sin\phi = \cos\phi\,\nabla\phi, \quad \nabla_\phi\cosh\phi = \sinh\phi\,\nabla\phi, \quad \nabla_\phi\sinh\phi = \cosh\phi\,\nabla\phi \] \[ \nabla_\phi\tan\phi = \nabla\phi\big(\cos^2\phi + \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1}, \qquad \nabla_\phi\cot\phi = -\nabla\phi\big(\sin^2\phi - \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1} \] \[ \nabla_\phi\tanh\phi = \nabla\phi\big(\cosh^2\phi - \tfrac{1}{2}\sinh(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1}, \qquad \nabla_\phi\coth\phi = -\nabla\phi\big(\sinh^2\phi - \tfrac{1}{2}\sinh(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1} \]

3. Inverse Trigonometric Selector Derivatives (\(u=\phi\), \(D_u \coloneqq \nabla_u/\nabla u\), SM pp. 246–249): \[ D_u\arccos u = -(1-u^2)^{-1/2}, \qquad D_u\arcsin u = (1-u^2)^{-1/2} \] \[ D_u\arctan u = \frac{1 + u\nabla\phi}{1 + u^2}, \qquad D_u\operatorname{arccot} u = -\frac{1 - u\nabla\phi}{1 + u^2} \]

4. Theorem 10.2 (Discrete Wronskian Determinant & Fundamental Systems, SM Eq. 82, p. 252): For an \(N\)-th order linear metronic selector difference equation: \[ Cy(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{\gamma=0}^N p_\gamma(\mathbf{n})\nabla^\gamma y(\mathbf{n}) = Q(\mathbf{n}) \tag{SM-82} \] a set of \(N\) solutions \(y_1(\mathbf{n}),\dots,y_N(\mathbf{n})\) forms a fundamental basis iff the discrete Wronskian determinant never vanishes: \[ D(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \det\!\left[\nabla^{\gamma-1} y_k(\mathbf{n})\right]_{N\times N} \ne 0 \quad \forall \mathbf{n} \in \mathbb{M}_\tau^1. \]

§10.1.5 Selectors (\(C_k\)), Vector Operator \(\bar{\delta}\) (SM-78–80) & Conceptual Bridge: * Oriented grid unit vectors \(\bar{\mathbf{e}}_i\) define \(\bar{\delta} \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \bar{\mathbf{e}}_i\nabla_i\) (SM Eqs. 78–80, pp. 223–235): \[ \bar{\delta}\phi = \operatorname{GRAD}_n\phi, \quad \operatorname{sp}(\bar{\delta}\mathbf{A}) = \operatorname{DIV}_n\mathbf{A}, \quad \bar{\delta}\wedge\mathbf{A} = \operatorname{ROT}_n\mathbf{A} \in \Omega_d^2(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n) \tag{SM-79b} \] * Conceptual Bridge: Like zooming in on a digital image until smooth curves resolve into pixels of area \(\tau\), Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC) replaces derivatives with causal backward differences while preserving exact global topological conservation laws (\(\operatorname{ROT}_n\operatorname{GRAD}_n \equiv \mathbf{0}\), \(\operatorname{DIV}_n\operatorname{ROT}_n \equiv 0\)).

Scholium 10.3 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Discrete Lattice Modules): Why formalize Metronic Calculus via \(\nabla_i = I - E_i^{-1}\) on \(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)\)? 1. Causal Directionality: \(\nabla\phi(n) = \phi(n) - \phi(n-1)\) measures change from historical predecessor \(n-1\) to \(n\). 2. Algebraic Telescoping: \(\nabla(\mathcal{S}\phi)(n) = \phi(n)\) without fractional boundary residuals. 3. DEC Topological Nilpotency: Cochain complexes \((\Omega_d^\bullet(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n), d_\tau)\) guarantee \(d_\tau^2 \equiv 0\).

Definition 10.4 (The Metronic Lattice Manifold \(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n\) and Shift Operators, Fig. 10.2): 1. Metronic Lattice Manifold: Isotropic uniform cubical mesh \(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n \coloneqq \bigoplus_{i=1}^n \sqrt{\tau}\,\mathbb{Z} = \{\sum_{i=1}^n n_i\sqrt{\tau}\,e_i \mid n_i \in \mathbb{Z}\} \subset \mathbb{R}^n\) with Banach algebra \((\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n), \|\cdot\|_\infty)\). 2. Lattice Shift Operators: Isometric automorphisms \((E_i\phi)(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \phi(\mathbf{n}+e_i)\) and backward shifts \(E_i^{-1}\). 3. Backward Difference Operator: \(\nabla_i \coloneqq I - E_i^{-1} \in \mathcal{B}(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n))\) with norm bound \(\|\nabla_i\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|I\|_{\mathrm{op}} + \|E_i^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}} = 2\).

§10.2: Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC) & Diskreter Hodge-Stern \(*_\tau\)

STRATUM A: PRIMAL-DUAL ORIENTATION (DEF. 10.5), DEC COCHAINS & HODGE LAPLACIAN (DEF. 10.6, FIG. 10.3) & LEAN 4 PROOF

Definition 10.5 (Primal-Dual Orientation and Discrete Hodge Stars): Let \(K\) be a regular cubical cell complex on \(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n\) and \(K^*\) its circumcentric Voronoi dual complex. Primal \(k\)-cells \(\sigma_k\) and dual \((n-k)\)-cells \(\sigma_{n-k}^*\) satisfy \(\operatorname{or}(\sigma_k)\wedge\operatorname{or}(\sigma_{n-k}^*) = (-1)^s\operatorname{or}(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)\) (\(s=0\) Riemannian, \(s=1\) Lorentzian). The Discrete Hodge Stars \(*_K \colon \Omega_d^k(K) \to \Omega_d^{n-k}(K^*)\) and \(*_{K^*} \colon \Omega_d^{n-k}(K^*) \to \Omega_d^k(K)\) are: \[ (*_K\omega)(\sigma_{n-k}^*) \coloneqq \frac{|\sigma_{n-k}^*|}{|\sigma_k|}\omega(\sigma_k), \qquad (*_{K^*}\theta)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq (-1)^{k(n-k)+s}\frac{|\sigma_k|}{|\sigma_{n-k}^*|}\theta(\sigma_{n-k}^*) \] satisfying exact involution duality: \(*_{K^*}\circ *_K = (-1)^{k(n-k)+s}\operatorname{id}_{\Omega_d^k(K)}\).

Definition 10.6 (Discrete Exterior Calculus on Metronic Lattices, Fig. 10.3): 1. Discrete \(k\)-Cochains: \(\Omega_d^k(K) \coloneqq \operatorname{Hom}(C_k(K), \mathbb{R})\). 2. Cubical Coboundary \(d_K \colon \Omega_d^k(K) \to \Omega_d^{k+1}(K)\): \[ (d_K\omega)(\square_{k+1}) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^{k+1}(-1)^i\big(\omega(\operatorname{Face}_i^+\square_{k+1}) - \omega(\operatorname{Face}_i^-\square_{k+1})\big), \quad d_K \circ d_K \equiv 0. \] 3. Discrete Codifferential: \(\delta_\tau \coloneqq (-1)^{n(k-1)+1+s}*_{K^*} d_{K^*} *_K\), satisfying \(\delta_\tau \circ \delta_\tau \equiv 0\). 4. Spatial Positive-Definite Hodge Laplacian: On a 3D Cauchy slice \(\Sigma_\tau \cong \mathbb{M}_\tau^3\) (\(s=0\)), \(\Delta_\tau\phi \coloneqq \delta_\tau d_\tau\phi \ge 0\) is strictly positive semi-definite.

namespace Syntrometrie.DEC_Proof -- Kernel-Checked S₂ Proof (Appendix C)
structure Grid2 where (x : ℤ) (y : ℤ) deriving DecidableEq
def shiftX (p : Grid2) : Grid2 := ⟨p.x - 1, p.y⟩
def shiftY (p : Grid2) : Grid2 := ⟨p.x, p.y - 1⟩
def Form0 := Grid2 → ℝ
structure Form1 where (dx : Grid2 → ℝ) (dy : Grid2 → ℝ)
def Form2 := Grid2 → ℝ
def d0 (f : Form0) : Form1 := ⟨fun p => f p - f (shiftX p), fun p => f p - f (shiftY p)⟩
def d1 (A : Form1) : Form2 := fun p => (A.dy p - A.dy (shiftX p)) - (A.dx p - A.dx (shiftY p))

theorem dec_coboundary_nilpotent (f : Form0) : d1 (d0 f) = (fun _ => 0) := by
  funext p; dsimp [d1, d0, shiftX, shiftY]; ring
end Syntrometrie.DEC_Proof

§10.3: Höhere Differenzen (SM-68), Monome & Stirling-Interpolation

STRATUM B: HIGHER DIFFERENCE BINOMIAL EXPANSION (THM. 10.7), POWER MONOMIALS (THM. 10.8), STIRLING & HONEYCOMB (FIG. 10.4)

Theorem 10.7 & Proof (Higher Difference Binomial Expansion, SM Eq. 68): For any \(k \in \mathbb{N}\), the \(k\)-th iterated backward difference \(\nabla_i^k = (I - E_i^{-1})^k\) satisfies: \[ \nabla_i^k\phi(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{\gamma=0}^k (-1)^\gamma \binom{k}{\gamma} E_i^{-\gamma}\phi(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{\gamma=0}^k (-1)^\gamma \binom{k}{\gamma}\phi(n_1,\dots,n_i-\gamma,\dots,n_n) \tag{SM-68} \] Proof: Express \(\nabla_i = I - E_i^{-1}\) in the Banach algebra \(\mathcal{B}(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n))\). Since \(I\) and \(E_i^{-1}\) commute (\(I \circ E_i^{-1} = E_i^{-1} \circ I\)), the binomial theorem applies directly term-by-term. \(\blacksquare\)

Theorem 10.8 (Metronic Difference of Power Monomials, SM pp. 222–223): For integers \(k, \gamma \ge 0\), the unit-step \(k\)-th backward difference of \(n^\gamma\) (\(0^0 = 1\)) is: \[ \nabla^k n^\gamma = \sum_{\ell=0}^k (-1)^\ell\binom{k}{\ell}(n-\ell)^\gamma = \begin{cases} \text{a polynomial of degree }\gamma - k, & k < \gamma, \\ \gamma!, & k = \gamma, \\ 0, & k > \gamma. \end{cases} \]

Remark (Stirling Expansion & Newton Interpolation) + Fig. 10.4 Honeycomb: With Stirling numbers of the second kind \(\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}\gamma\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right\}\), \(\nabla^k n^\gamma = \sum_{j=k}^\gamma \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}\gamma\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right\} j^{\underline{k}}(n-k)^{\underline{j-k}}\) and \((\nabla^k n^\gamma)_{n=0} = (-1)^{\gamma-k}k!\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}\gamma\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right\}\), yielding Newton’s exact finite interpolation \(f(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}(\nabla^k f)(k)\) for \(n \ge 0\). §10.3: Diskrete Leibniz-Produkt-/Quotientenregeln & Pseudokettenregel

STRATUM B: SCHOLIUM 10.9, PSEUDOCHAIN RULE (PROP. 10.10, THM. 10.11, SM-75) & DISCRETE LEIBNIZ PROOF (THM. 10.12, SM-68a)

Scholium 10.9 (The Discrete Leibniz Cross-Term): Backward differences obey \(\nabla(uv) = u\nabla v + v\nabla u - (\nabla u)(\nabla v)\). The final term records the finite lattice step and vanishes in the continuum limit, making the discrete product law transparent.

Proposition 10.10 & Theorem 10.11 (Metronic Coordinate Transformation & Pseudochain Rule, SM Eq. 75, p. 227): For a lattice function represented through intermediate variables \(\psi_1,\dots,\psi_\Lambda\), Heim writes the total metronic difference as: \[ \nabla\Phi = \sum_{k=1}^\Lambda \Phi_{(\psi_k)}\nabla\psi_k, \qquad \Phi_{(\psi_k)} \coloneqq \frac{\nabla_{(\psi_k)}\Phi}{\nabla\psi_k} \tag{SM-75} \] Because these are finite increments, the quotient \(\Phi_{(\psi_k)}\) is direction-dependent and must be evaluated using the stated lattice difference convention; it is not automatically the classical infinitesimal chain rule.

Theorem 10.12 (Discrete Leibniz Product and Quotient Rules, SM Eq. 68a): For any lattice sequences \(u, v \in \ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)\), \(\nabla_i = I - E_i^{-1}\) satisfies: \[ \nabla_i(uv) = (\nabla_i u)v + (E_i^{-1}u)(\nabla_i v) = (\nabla_i u)v + u(\nabla_i v) - (\nabla_i u)(\nabla_i v) \tag{SM-68a} \] \[ \nabla_i(uv^{-1}) = (\nabla_i u)v^{-1} - (E_i^{-1}u)v^{-1}(\nabla_i v)(E_i^{-1}v)^{-1} \quad (v(\mathbf{n}) \ne 0\;\forall\mathbf{n}) \] Strict left-to-right ordering is mandatory when \(u, v\) are non-commutative spin-rotor matrix fields (\(\hat{s}\)).

Proof of Theorem 10.12 (4-Step Non-Commutative Derivation): 1. Expand \(\nabla_i(uv)(\mathbf{n}) = u(\mathbf{n})v(\mathbf{n}) - u(\mathbf{n}-e_i)v(\mathbf{n}-e_i)\). 2. Add and subtract \(u(\mathbf{n}-e_i)v(\mathbf{n})\) (or \(u(\mathbf{n})v(\mathbf{n}-e_i)\)): \(\nabla_i(uv) = (\nabla_i u)v + (E_i^{-1}u)(\nabla_i v) = u(\nabla_i v) + (E_i^{-1}v)(\nabla_i u)\). 3. Substitute \(E_i^{-1}u = u - \nabla_i u\) to obtain \((\nabla_i u)v + u(\nabla_i v) - (\nabla_i u)(\nabla_i v)\). 4. For \(v^{-1}\), \(\nabla_i(v^{-1}) = v^{-1} - (E_i^{-1}v)^{-1} = -v^{-1}(\nabla_i v)(E_i^{-1}v)^{-1}\). Applying the product rule to \(u\cdot v^{-1}\) yields the exact non-commutative quotient rule. \(\blacksquare\)

§10.3: Hauptsatz der Diskreten Analysis & Kontinuumslimit (\(\tau \to 0^+\))

STRATUM B: DISCRETE SUMMATION (DEF. 10.13), FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM (THM. 10.14) & CONTINUUM LIMIT PROOF (THM. 10.15)

Definition 10.13 (The Discrete Summation Operator \(\mathcal{S}\)) & Theorem 10.14 (Fundamental Theorem of Discrete Calculus): * Def. 10.13: Anchored indefinite sum \((\mathcal{S}_{n_0}\phi)(n) \coloneqq \sum_{j=n_0}^n \phi(j)\) on \(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{Z})\), \((\mathcal{S}_{-\infty}\phi)(n) \coloneqq \sum_{j=-\infty}^n \phi(j)\) on \(\ell^1(\mathbb{Z})\), and definite sum \(\mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2}\phi \coloneqq \sum_{j=n_1}^{n_2}\phi(j)\). * Thm. 10.14: Let \(\phi \in \ell^1(\mathbb{Z})\) and \(\Phi \in \ell^\infty(\mathbb{Z})\) satisfy \(\nabla\Phi = \phi\). Then: 1. \(\nabla(\mathcal{S}\phi)(n) = \phi(n)\) and \(\mathcal{S}(\nabla\Phi)(n) = \Phi(n) - \lim_{j\to-\infty}\Phi(j)\). 2. Telescoping definite sum: \[ \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2}\phi = \sum_{j=n_1}^{n_2}\big(\Phi(j) - \Phi(j-1)\big) = \Phi(n_2) - \Phi(n_1 - 1) \tag{SM-67a} \] Proof: \(\nabla(\mathcal{S}\phi)(n) = \sum_{j=-\infty}^n \phi(j) - \sum_{j=-\infty}^{n-1}\phi(j) = \phi(n)\); telescoping is immediate. \(\blacksquare\)

Worked Example (1D Power Difference & Telescoping Sum) + Lean 4 Proof: For \(\Phi(n) = n^2\) on \(\mathbb{M}_\tau^1 = \mathbb{Z}\), \(\phi(n) = \nabla(n^2) = n^2 - (n-1)^2 = 2n - 1\). Summing from \(n=1\) to \(N\) gives \(\mathcal{S}_1^N(2n-1) = 2\frac{N(N+1)}{2} - N = N^2 = \Phi(N) - \Phi(0)\).

Theorem 10.15 (Continuum Correspondence Limit Theorem): Let \(f \in C^2(\mathbb{R})\) with bounded second derivative, and sample \(\phi_\tau(n) \coloneqq f(n\tau)\) on \(\mathbb{M}_\tau^1 = \tau\mathbb{Z}\). 1. Derivative Convergence: For any fixed \(x = n\tau \in \mathbb{R}\): \[ \lim_{\tau\to 0^+} \frac{(\nabla\phi_\tau)(n)}{\tau} = \lim_{\tau\to 0^+} \frac{f(x) - f(x-\tau)}{\tau} = f'(x), \qquad \left|\frac{\nabla\phi_\tau(n)}{\tau} - f'(x)\right| \le \frac{\tau}{2}\|f''\|_\infty. \] 2. Integral Convergence: For \([a, b]\) with \(a = n_1\tau, b = n_2\tau\): \[ \lim_{\tau\to 0^+} \tau\sum_{j=n_1}^{n_2} \phi_\tau(j) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx. \]

Proof of Theorem 10.15 (Taylor Integral Remainder Bound): By Taylor’s theorem with integral remainder, \(f(x-\tau) = f(x) - \tau f'(x) + \int_{x-\tau}^x (t - x + \tau)f''(t)\,dt\). Dividing by \(\tau\) yields \(\left|\frac{f(x)-f(x-\tau)}{\tau} - f'(x)\right| = \frac{1}{\tau}\left|\int_{x-\tau}^x (t-x+\tau)f''(t)\,dt\right| \le \frac{\tau}{2}\|f''\|_\infty \to 0\) as \(\tau \to 0^+\). Part (2) is the convergence of Riemann sums to the Riemann integral. \(\blacksquare\)

§10.3: Cubical FEEC, Whitney–de Rham Isomorphie & UV-Cutoff \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}}\)

STRATUM B: CUBICAL FEEC (THM. 10.18), DE RHAM ISOMORPHISM (THM. 10.19, DEF. 10.20) & UV DISPERSION PROOF (THM. 10.21)

Theorem 10.18 (Cubical Finite Element Exterior Calculus (FEEC) Convergence): On a uniform cubical mesh \(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n\) with trimmed-polynomial subcomplex \(\mathcal{W}_\tau^k(K) \coloneqq \mathcal{P}_{1,\dots,1}^-\Omega^k(K)\) (Arnold et al. 2006; Boffi et al. 2013), smoothed commuting projections \(\Pi_\tau^k \colon L^2\Omega^k \to \mathcal{W}_\tau^k(K)\) satisfy: \[ d \circ \Pi_\tau^k = \Pi_\tau^{k+1} \circ d, \qquad \|\Pi_\tau^k\alpha\|_{L^2} \le C_{\mathrm{proj}}\|\alpha\|_{L^2}, \qquad \|\Pi_\tau^k\alpha - \alpha\|_{L^2} \le C_{\mathrm{approx}}\,\tau^s\|\alpha\|_{H^s} \quad (0 < s \le 1). \] * Claim Ceiling (\(c_{\mathrm{FEEC}}\)): The cubical FEEC construction is a valid mathematical approximation theorem in \(L^2\); it does not by itself prove that physical spacetime is discrete.

Theorem 10.19 (Metronic Cubical de Rham Cohomology Isomorphism) & Definition 10.20 (\(R_\tau, W_\tau\)): The de Rham Integration Map \((R_\tau\omega)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq \int_{\sigma_k}\omega\) and Whitney Interpolation Map \((W_\tau c)(\mathbf{x}) \coloneqq k!\sum c([v_{i_0},\dots,v_{i_k}])\sum_{j=0}^k (-1)^j \mu_{i_j} d\mu_{i_0}\wedge\dots\wedge\widehat{d\mu_{i_j}}\wedge\dots\wedge d\mu_{i_k}\) satisfy: \[ d \circ W_\tau = W_\tau \circ d_\tau, \quad R_\tau \circ W_\tau = \operatorname{id}_{\Omega_d^k(K)} \implies H^k\big(\Omega_d^\bullet(K), d_\tau\big) \cong H_{\mathrm{dR}}^k(|\Omega|) \cong H_{\mathrm{sing}}^k(|\Omega|; \mathbb{R}). \] This isomorphism is metric-independent, preserving topological quantum numbers (Chern/magnetic flux charges) exactly on the lattice.

Theorem 10.21 & Proof (Metronic Lattice Momentum Dispersion and UV Cutoff): 1. Fourier Diagonalization: \(\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i\phi)(\mathbf{k}) = (1 - e^{-\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i})\widehat{\phi}(\mathbf{k})\) and \(\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i^*\phi) = (e^{\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i}-1)\widehat{\phi}\). 2. Positive DEC 0-Laplacian Dispersion (\(\Delta_\tau = \sum_i \tau_i^{-2}\nabla_i^*\nabla_i\)): \[ \lambda(\mathbf{k}) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\tau_i^2}(2 - 2\cos(k_i\tau_i)) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{4}{\tau_i^2}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{k_i\tau_i}{2}\right) \ge 0. \] 3. UV Cutoff & Torus Spectral Gap: On \(\mathbb{Z}^4\), \(\sigma(\Delta_\tau) = [0, 16/\tau^2]\), giving ultraviolet scale \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}} = 4/\sqrt{\tau}\); on a periodic \(N\)-torus, \(\Delta E_{\min} = \frac{4}{\tau_1^2}\sin^2(\pi/N) > 0\) (whereas an intrinsic mass gap requires a mass term in \(V_{\mathrm{gauge}}\) or compact holonomy). \(\blacksquare\)

Operadic Feature Consumption via the Episyllogismus (\(k \uparrow\), §12.2.1, Figs. 12.7–12.9): * Higher cortical tiers do not maintain an uncompressed pixel buffer of lower sensory arrays. Within the completed colored Banach operad \(\Osyn\) (Ch. 2), multi-channel integration across levels is governed by: \[ \ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1} \colon \Osyn(\underbrace{\gamma,\dots,\gamma}_{m\text{ times}};\; \gamma+1) \;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi\; \left(F_\gamma \;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi\; F_\gamma\right) \longrightarrow F_{\gamma+1} \] * Input activations at tier \(\gamma\) (V1 Gabor orientations, spatial frequencies, motion vectors, A1 pitch bands) function strictly as operands, projected into the coinvariant quotient space: \[ F_{\gamma+1} \;\cong\; \left(F_\gamma^{\;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m}\right) \Big/ \overline{\operatorname{span}}\big\{u - \sigma(u) \;\big|\; \sigma \in \Sigma_m\big\} \Big/ \mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{relations}} \]

Theorem 12.6 & Proof (Operadic Information Erasure Theorem): Let \(F_\gamma\) be an \(n\)-dimensional real Banach space representing a lower cortical feature map. Under \(\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1}\), input coordinates \((x_1, \dots, x_m) \in (F_\gamma)^m\) are algebraically consumed into the coinvariant quotient. For any \(n \ge 2\) and \(m \ge 2\), the evaluation kernel satisfies: \[ \boxed{\dim\big(\ker(\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1})\big) \;\ge\; n^m \;-\; \binom{n + m - 1}{m} \;>\; 0} \] Proof: The evaluation morphism factors through the symmetrized coinvariant projection \(\pi_{\mathrm{sym}} \colon (F_\gamma)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m} \twoheadrightarrow \Sym^m(F_\gamma)\), whose kernel is spanned by all non-symmetric tensor permutations. In finite dimensions, \(\dim(F_\gamma^{\otimes m}) = n^m\) while \(\dim(\Sym^m(F_\gamma)) = \binom{n+m-1}{m}\). For all \(n \ge 2, m \ge 2\), \(n^m - \binom{n+m-1}{m} > 0\). Because \(\ev\) factors through \(\pi_{\mathrm{sym}}\), \(\ker(\pi_{\mathrm{sym}}) \subseteq \ker(\ev)\), erasing individual lower coordinates unless an explicit top-down adjoint section \(\ev^*\) is applied. \(\blacksquare\)

Tri-Adjoint Quantifiers (Prop. 12.22) & Beck–Chevalley Invariance (Thm. 12.23, §12.3.6): * Prop. 12.22: For every \(f \colon V \to U\) in \(\Ctx\), pullback \(f^* \colon \Sub_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbf{y}U) \to \Sub_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbf{y}V)\) admits left and right adjoints \(\exists_f \dashv f^* \dashv \forall_f\), with \(\exists_f(A) \coloneqq \Im(f \circ \iota_A)\) and \(\forall_f(A) \coloneqq \max\{B \hookrightarrow \mathbf{y}U \mid f^*(B) \le A\}\). * Theorem 12.23 & Proof (Beck–Chevalley Invariance): Over pullback \(W = V_1 \times_U V_2\) with \(\pi_1 \colon W \to V_1, \pi_2 \colon W \to V_2\) and \(g \colon V_1 \to U, f \colon V_2 \to U\), for every \(A \hookrightarrow \mathbf{y}V_2\): \[ \mathbf{BC}_\exists \colon \;\exists_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*(A)) \;\cong\; g^*(\exists_f(A)), \qquad \mathbf{BC}_\forall \colon \;g^*(\forall_f(A)) \;\cong\; \forall_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*(A)) \] Proof: (\(\mathbf{BC}_\exists\)) Since \(\Esyn\) is a Grothendieck topos, regular images are stable under pullback, so pulling back \(A \twoheadrightarrow \exists_f(A) \hookrightarrow \mathbf{y}U\) along \(\mathbf{y}g^*\) yields \(\exists_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*A) \cong g^*(\exists_f A)\). (\(\mathbf{BC}_\forall\)) By categorical mates: \(\Hom(B, g^*(\forall_f A)) \cong \Hom(f^*(\exists_g B), A) \cong \Hom(\exists_{\pi_2}(\pi_1^*B), A) \cong \Hom(B, \forall_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*A))\), plus Yoneda. \(\blacksquare\)

World \((U, k)\) satisfies: \[ (U, k) \models \Stable_{j+1}(P') \iff (U, k) \models P' \;\wedge\; \forall X\big(\IGP_{j+1}(X, P') \implies (U, k) \models \Stable_j(X)\big) \] * Theorem 12.25 & Proof (Working Memory Invariance): If \(S(x); \Gamma \vdash^k \Stable_k(P)\), then for every \(\alpha \colon V \to U\) in \(\Ctx\), \(U \Vdash P \implies V \Vdash \alpha^*(P)\). Theorem 12.26 & Proof (Simultaneous Multi-Level Prime Saturation Theorem, §12.3.8): Let \(S(x); \Gamma_0 \nvdash^0 \phi_0\) be an unprovable root sequent at level \(k=0\). There exists an infinite sequence of Prime Saturated Theories \(\mathbf{\Delta} \coloneqq \langle \Delta_k \subset \mathcal{L}_k \rangle_{k \in \mathbb{N}_0}\) linked by the deterministic dynamic transition relation: \[ (\Delta_k, k) \,R_{\pi_F}^c\, (\Delta_{k+1}, k+1) \;\iff\; \big\{\theta \in \mathcal{L}_{k+1} \;\big|\; [\pi_F]\theta \in \Delta_k\big\} \;\subseteq\; \Delta_{k+1} \] satisfying the Truth Lemma across all levels \(k \in \mathbb{N}_0\): \[ \boxed{(\Delta_k, k) \models \psi \;\iff\; \psi \in \Delta_k \qquad \forall \psi \in \mathcal{L}_k} \] Proof: Extend \(\Gamma_0\) to a prime \(0\)-theory \(\Delta_0\) with \(\phi_0 \notin \Delta_0\) via the Prime Extension Lemma. Inductively, given \(\Delta_k\), define \(\Theta_{k+1} \coloneqq \{\theta \mid [\pi_F]\theta \in \Delta_k\} \cup F_{\mathrm{ops}}(\Delta_k \cap \Prop_k)\). If \(\Theta_{k+1} \vdash^{k+1} \bot\), rule \(([\pi_F]\text{-Unstep})\) forces \(\Delta_k \vdash^k [\pi_F]\bot \to \bot\), contradicting consistency of \(\Delta_k\). Thus \(\Theta_{k+1}\) extends to a prime \((k+1)\)-theory \(\Delta_{k+1}\), and Truth Lemma induction holds on lexicographic rank \(\mathbf{m}(\psi) = (\operatorname{rk}(\psi), k)\). \(\blacksquare\)

§12.4.1–12.4.2: Completed Operad \(\Osyn\), Beck Distributive Law & Selection Functors

Definition 12.27: Completed Free Colored Banach Operad \(\Osyn\) (§12.4.1) Let \(E_{\mathrm{pyr}} \in \mathsf{Coll}_{\mathbf{Col}}(\mathbf{Ban})\) be the colored generating collection with operations \(E_{\mathrm{pyr}}(\gamma,\dots,\gamma;\gamma+1) \coloneqq \mathcal{B}_{\le 1}((F_\gamma)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m}, F_{\gamma+1})\) and \(\{0\}\) otherwise. The Completed Free Operad is: \[ \Osyn \;\coloneqq\; \widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\pi(E_{\mathrm{pyr}})(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma) \;\coloneqq\; \bigoplus_{[\tau] \in \operatorname{Tree}(\vec{\gamma};\gamma)/\sim}^{\ell^1} \left(\widehat{\bigotimes}_{v \in V(\tau)}^\pi E_{\mathrm{pyr}}\big(\operatorname{in}(v); \operatorname{out}(v)\big)\right)_{\Aut(\tau)} \]

Theorem 12.28 & Proof (Inductive Proof of the Beck Distributive Law for Tree Monads): Let \((\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \eta_{\mathrm{pyr}})\) and \((\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}, \mu_{\mathrm{frag}}, \eta_{\mathrm{frag}})\) be the algebraic free tree monads on \(\FinBan\). The natural transformation \(\lambda \colon \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}} \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \Longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\) defined by structural recursion: \[ \lambda_X\big(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(t)\big) \coloneqq \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}})(t), \qquad \lambda_X\big(\psi(t_1,\dots,t_m)\big) \coloneqq \mu_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\psi)\big(\lambda_X(t_1),\dots,\lambda_X(t_m)\big) \] satisfies the four Beck coherence diagrams identically: 1. Unit Law 1 (\(\lambda \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\eta_{\mathrm{frag}} = \eta_{\mathrm{frag}}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\)): \(\lambda_X(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(\eta_{\mathrm{frag}}(x))) = \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}})(\eta_{\mathrm{frag}}(x)) = \eta_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(x))\). 2. Unit Law 2 (\(\lambda \circ \eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} = \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}\)): Holds directly by the base definition. 3. Multiplication Law 1 (\(\mu_{\mathrm{frag}}\) Pentagon): Naturality of operadic substitution \(\psi \circ_i \theta\) commutes with root grafting in \(\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\). 4. Multiplication Law 2 (\(\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}\) Pentagon): Induction on tree depth + associativity of \(\widehat{\otimes}_\pi\) gives \(\lambda_X(\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}(T)) = (\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ (\lambda\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ (\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\lambda)(T)\), extending continuously via the BLT Theorem to \(T_{\mathrm{pyr}}, T_{\mathrm{frag}}\). \(\blacksquare\)

Definition 12.29: The Four Elementary Selection Power Functors in \(\FinBan\) (§12.4.2) For an \(n\)-dimensional carrier space \(V \in \Obj(\FinBan)\), the four universal selection functors of arity \(m\) are: \[ \begin{aligned} \mathsf{Sel}_{(4)}^{(m)}(V) &\coloneqq V^{\otimes m}, & \dim &= n^m & &\text{(Homometral Asymmetric)} \\ \mathsf{Sel}_{(2)}^{(m)}(V, B) &\coloneqq V^{\underline{\otimes}m}(B), & \dim &= \frac{n!}{(n-m)!} & &\text{(Heterometral Asymmetric)} \\ \mathsf{Sel}_{(3)}^{(m)}(V) &\coloneqq \Sym^m(V), & \dim &= \binom{n+m-1}{m} & &\text{(Homometral Symmetric)} \\ \mathsf{Sel}_{(1)}^{(m)}(V, B) &\coloneqq \Lambda^m(V), & \dim &= \binom{n}{m} & &\text{(Heterometral Alternating)} \end{aligned} \]

Role of the Four Selection Regimes in Cortical Syntax Compression: * \(\mathsf{Sel}_{(4)}^{(m)}\) preserves full ordered sequence syntax (\(n^m\)). * \(\mathsf{Sel}_{(3)}^{(m)} = \Sym^m(V)\) drives Operadic Feature Consumption (Thm. 12.6), projecting out permutation order to form order-invariant perceptual gestalts. * \(\mathsf{Sel}_{(1)}^{(m)} = \Lambda^m(V)\) drives Programmable Cognitive Closure (Syndromabschluss, Thm. 12.34), vanishing identically whenever \(m > n\).

§13.1.1: Metric-Affine Qualia Geometry & Non-Abelian Stokes–Wilson Holonomy

STRATA A & B: METRIC-AFFINE CURVATURE DECOMPOSITION & WILSON HOLONOMY (DEF. 13.1 – THM. 13.2)

Definition 13.1 (Metric-Affine Manifold Structure): Let \(M_U\) be a cognitive context manifold equipped with generalized non-Hermitian metric \({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = g + \omega\) (Riemannian metric \(g\) + skew-symmetric torsion/vorticity 2-form \(\omega\)). On principal bundle \(P_U \to M_U\) with connection \(\mathbf{A} = A_0 + \sum a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}\), the total curvature decomposes as: \[ F_A \;=\; \sum_k \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \;+\; \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \]

Theorem 13.2 (Non-Abelian Stokes–Wilson Holonomy for Bound Qualia): Let \(P_U \to M_U\) be a principal \(G\)-bundle over an orientable cognitive context manifold \(M_U\) with connection \(\mathbf{A} = A_0 + a_1 + a_2 \in \Omega^1(M_U, \mathfrak{g})\) where \(a_1 \wedge a_2 \ne 0\), and let \(\mathcal{C} = \partial \Sigma\) bound a compact 2-surface \(\Sigma \subset M_U\):

  1. Wilson Loop Holonomy: \(\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathcal{C}) \coloneqq \mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A}\right) \coloneqq \lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{k=1}^N \exp\!\left(-\mathbf{A}(\dot{\gamma}(t_k))\Delta t\right)\).
  2. Non-Abelian Stokes Theorem: \(\tr\!\left(\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathcal{C})\right) = \tr\!\left(\mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} F_A\right)\right) = \tr\!\left(\mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} (\mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2])\right)\right)\).
  3. Pure Quale Commutator Phase Shift (\(\mathcal{F}_1 = 0, \mathcal{F}_2 = 0\)): \[ \Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\partial \Sigma) \;=\; \mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} [a_1, a_2]\right) \;\ne\; \id_G \]

Proof of Theorem 13.2 (Dyson Series & Plaquette Commutator): Parallel transport \(\Gamma(t) \in G\) along \(\gamma \colon [0,1] \to M_U\) satisfies \(\frac{d}{dt}\Gamma(t) + \mathbf{A}(\dot{\gamma}(t))\Gamma(t) = 0\) with \(\Gamma(0) = \id\), solved by the Dyson path-ordered series \(\Gamma(1) = \id + \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n \int_0^1 dt_1 \dots \int_0^{t_{n-1}} dt_n \, \mathbf{A}(t_1)\dots\mathbf{A}(t_n)\). Subdividing \(\Sigma\) into plaquettes \(\delta\sigma_{ij} = \Delta x^i \wedge \Delta x^j\), orthogonal transport commutators yield \(\Gamma_{\Delta x^i}^{-1}\Gamma_{\Delta x^j}^{-1}\Gamma_{\Delta x^i}\Gamma_{\Delta x^j} = \id - F_{ij}\Delta x^i\Delta x^j + \mathcal{O}(|\Delta x|^3)\). Surface integration gives \(\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\partial\Sigma) = \mathcal{P}\exp(-\iint_\Sigma (\mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2]))\). \(\blacksquare\)

§13.2.1: Telecentric Morse Separatrices & DeTurck Parabolic Smoothing

STRATUM A & B: LYAPUNOV STABILITY & DETURCK SOBOLEV CONTRACTION PROOF (THM. 13.9 – THM. 13.10)

Theorem 13.9 (Morse Separatrices & Televariant Lyapunov Stability): On complete Riemannian manifold \((\MAR, \gAR)\), the Extinktionsdiskriminante \(\Dext \coloneqq \partial\mathcal{B}(T_z) = \bigcup_{j=1}^M W^s(p_j)\) is an invariant codimension-1 stable manifold of index-1 hyperbolic saddles separating the televariant attractor basin \(\mathcal{B}(T_z)\) from dysvariant collapse into \(\nullsyntrix\). Within \(\mathcal{B}(T_z)\), the Lyapunov potential \(V(x) \coloneqq \Psi(x) - \Psi(T_z)\) satisfies exponential dissipation \(V(\Phi_t(x_0)) \le V(x_0)e^{-2\gamma t}\).

Theorem 13.10 (DeTurck Parabolic Smoothing & Sobolev Fixed-Point Contraction): Let \(\mathcal{M}\) be a compact smooth \(n\)-manifold (\(\partial\mathcal{M}=\emptyset\)). Define the non-linear Ricci-like operator: \[ \mathcal{T}(g)_{ij} \;\coloneqq\; -2R_{ij}(g) + \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i, \qquad V^k \coloneqq g^{pq}\!\left(\Gamma_{pq}^k(g) - \widetilde{\Gamma}_{pq}^k\right) \] For Sobolev index \(s > \frac{n}{2} + 2\), the heat-smoothed cascade operator \(\mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}} \coloneqq e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_g + c_0 I)} \circ \mathcal{T}\) is a strict contraction on \(\mathbf{B}_{H^s}(g_0, \delta) \subset H^s(\mathcal{M}, \Sym^2(T^*\mathcal{M}))\): \[ \|\mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g_1) - \mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g_2)\|_{H^s} \;\le\; k_M \|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s} \quad (k_M < 1) \] converging uniquely to a smooth stationary apex metric \({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\).

Four-Step Proof of Theorem 13.10:

  1. Strong Ellipticity: The DeTurck term kills diffeomorphism gauge degeneracy; principal symbol \(\sigma_\xi(\mathcal{T}(g))h_{ij} = g^{ab}\xi_a\xi_b h_{ij} = \|\xi\|_g^2 h_{ij}\) maps \(H^s(\mathcal{M}) \to H^{s-2}(\mathcal{M})\).
  2. Banach Algebra Lipschitz Bound: Since \(s > n/2 + 2\), \(H^s(\mathcal{M}) \hookrightarrow C^2(\mathcal{M})\) is a Banach algebra, giving \(\|\mathcal{T}(g_1) - \mathcal{T}(g_2)\|_{H^{s-2}} \le C_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)\|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s}\).
  3. Parabolic Smoothing: \(\|e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_g + c_0 I)}\|_{\mathcal{B}(H^{s-2}, H^s)} \le C_{\mathrm{heat}} \frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} \implies k_M \coloneqq C_{\mathrm{heat}}C_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)\frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} < 1\) for large \(\tau_M\).
  4. Banach Fixed Point & Bootstrapping: \(g^{(n+1)} = \mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g^{(n)}) \to {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\) by elliptic regularity. \(\blacksquare\)

Theorem 13.19 (Commutativity of the Stokes–Cartan Discretization Functor): Let \(K\) be a regular cubical cell complex discretizing smooth orientable manifold \(\mathcal{M}_n\) at scale \(h > 0\). The de Rham integration projection \((\mathcal{R}_h^k \omega)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq \int_{\sigma_k} \omega\) commutes strictly with the discrete coboundary \(d_h\) in \(\mathbf{Ch}_{\ge 0}(\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})\): \[ d_h \circ \mathcal{R}_h^k \;=\; \mathcal{R}_h^{k+1} \circ d, \qquad \|\Pi_h^k \alpha - \alpha\|_{L^2} \;\le\; C_{\mathrm{approx}}\, h^s \|\alpha\|_{H^s} \;\; (0 < s \le 1) \] 3-Step Proof: For \((k+1)\)-cell \(\sigma_{k+1}\) with boundary \(\partial\sigma_{k+1} = \sum_j (-1)^j \operatorname{Face}_j(\sigma_{k+1})\): (1) \(((\mathcal{R}_h^{k+1}\circ d)\omega)(\sigma_{k+1}) = \int_{\sigma_{k+1}} d\omega\); (2) \(((d_h \circ \mathcal{R}_h^k)\omega)(\sigma_{k+1}) = (\mathcal{R}_h^k\omega)(\partial\sigma_{k+1}) = \int_{\partial\sigma_{k+1}}\omega\); (3) Classical Stokes’ Theorem \(\int_{\sigma_{k+1}} d\omega = \int_{\partial\sigma_{k+1}}\omega\) equates both paths. \(\blacksquare\)

UV Cutoff & Torus IR Gap: On \(\mathbb{Z}^4\), \(\sigma(\Delta_\tau) = [0, 16/\tau^2]\) gives ultraviolet cutoff \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}} = 4/\sqrt{\tau}\); on a finite periodic \(N\)-torus (\(k_i = \frac{2\pi m_i}{N\tau_i}\)), the lowest non-zero mode \(\mathbf{m}=(1,0,\dots,0)\) has strictly positive gap \(\Delta E_{\min} = \frac{4}{\tau_1^2}\sin^2(\pi/N) > 0\).

§13.6.1: The Geometry of Self-Consciousness & Lawvere Fixed Points

STRATA A & B: CURRY–HOWARD PROOF OF THE LAWVERE EGO FIXED-POINT THEOREM (THM. 13.24)

Resolving the Homuncular Regress of Ich-Bewusstsein

  • How does a cognitive system achieve self-awareness (Ich-Bewusstsein) without triggering an infinite homuncular regress (an observer observing an observer observing…)?
  • Following F. William Lawvere’s (1969) categorical diagonal theorem, self-consciousness is not a separate meta-module, but the invariant diagonal fixed point \(e^* \colon \mathbf{1} \to A\) of the internal evaluation morphism in a cartesian closed category (CCC).

Theorem 13.24 (Curry–Howard Categorical Proof of the Lawvere Ego Fixed Point): Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a cartesian closed category with terminal object \(\mathbf{1}\), internal evaluation object \(\Omega\), and observer internal state space \(A \in \Obj(\mathcal{C})\). If an internal evaluation morphism \(\Phi \colon A \times A \to \Omega\) is point-surjective (its curried transpose \(\hat{\Phi} \colon A \to \Omega^A\) has a right section on global elements), then every endomorphism \(f \colon \Omega \to \Omega\) possesses a fixed point \(y^* \in \Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \Omega)\): \[ f \circ y^* \;=\; y^* \] In particular, the self-reflective diagonal \(\Delta_A \colon A \to A \times A\) induces an invariant self-representation (Ego Token) \(e^* \in \Hom(\mathbf{1}, A)\) satisfying: \[ \Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle \;=\; f\!\left(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle\right) \]

Complete Three-Step Diagram-Chase Proof of Theorem 13.24:

  • Step 1 (Construction of the Diagonal Functional): Let \(\Delta_A \coloneqq \langle \id_A, \id_A \rangle \colon A \to A \times A\) be the canonical diagonal morphism. Define the self-evaluating diagonal arrow \(\delta \coloneqq \Phi \circ \Delta_A \colon A \to \Omega\). Post-composing with \(f \colon \Omega \to \Omega\) yields the modified diagonal functional: \[ g \;\coloneqq\; f \circ \delta \;=\; f \circ \Phi \circ \langle \id_A, \id_A \rangle \;\colon\; A \longrightarrow \Omega \]
  • Step 2 (Currying & Surjectivity Inversion): By cartesian closure, \(\Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(A \times A, \Omega) \cong \Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(A, \Omega^A)\) via exponential transpose \(\hat{\Phi} \colon A \to \Omega^A\). The arrow \(g \colon A \to \Omega\) corresponds under adjunction to a global element \(\ulcorner g \urcorner \colon \mathbf{1} \to \Omega^A\). By point-surjectivity of \(\hat{\Phi}\) on global elements \(\Hom(\mathbf{1}, A) \to \Hom(\mathbf{1}, \Omega^A)\), there exists a representing global element (the Ego Token \(e^*\)): \[ e^* \;\colon\; \mathbf{1} \longrightarrow A \quad \text{such that} \quad \hat{\Phi} \circ e^* \;=\; \ulcorner g \urcorner \]
  • Step 3 (Evaluation Along the Diagonal): Uncurrying \(\hat{\Phi} \circ e^* = \ulcorner g \urcorner\) implies that for all generalized elements \(x \colon X \to A\): \[ \Phi \circ \langle e^* \circ !_X, \; x \rangle \;=\; g \circ x \;=\; f \circ \Phi \circ \langle x, x \rangle \] Instantiating \(X \coloneqq \mathbf{1}\) and setting \(x \coloneqq e^* \colon \mathbf{1} \to A\) yields \(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle = f(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle)\). Setting \(y^* \coloneqq \Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle \colon \mathbf{1} \to \Omega\) gives \(f \circ y^* = y^*\). \(\blacksquare\)

import Mathlib
open CategoryTheory
namespace Syntrometrie.CognitiveArchitecture

structure ContextObject where
  D : Type
  P : Type
  C : Type
  [instD : NormedAddCommGroup D] [instDSpace : NormedSpace ℝ D] [instDFin : FiniteDimensional ℝ D]
  [instP : NormedAddCommGroup P] [instPSpace : NormedSpace ℝ P] [instPFin : FiniteDimensional ℝ P]
  [instC : NormedAddCommGroup C] [instCSpace : NormedSpace ℝ C] [instCFin : FiniteDimensional ℝ C]
  K : D →L[ℝ] (P →L[ℝ] C)
  K_contr : ‖K‖ ≤ 1
  z : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] P
  zeta : D ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] D

structure ContextHom (U V : ContextObject) where
  alpha_D : U.D →L[ℝ] V.D
  alpha_D_contractive : ‖alpha_D‖ ≤ 1
  alpha_P : U.P →L[ℝ] V.P
  alpha_P_contractive : ‖alpha_P‖ ≤ 1
  alpha_C : U.C →L[ℝ] V.C
  alpha_C_contractive : ‖alpha_C‖ ≤ 1
  comm : ∀ (d : U.D) (p : U.P), alpha_C (U.K d p) = V.K (alpha_D d) (alpha_P p)
  cipher_z : ∀ p, alpha_P (U.z p) = V.z (alpha_P p)
  cipher_zeta : ∀ d, alpha_D (U.zeta d) = V.zeta (alpha_D d)
lemma opNorm_comp_le_one {E F G : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
    (f : E →L[ℝ] F) (g : F →L[ℝ] G) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) (hg : ‖g‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖g.comp f‖ ≤ 1 := by
  calc ‖g.comp f‖ ≤ ‖g‖ * ‖f‖ := ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le g f
    _ ≤ 1 * 1 := mul_le_mul hg hf (norm_nonneg f) zero_le_one
    _ = 1 := mul_one 1

instance : Category ContextObject where
  Hom U V := ContextHom U V
  id U := {
    alpha_D := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.D, alpha_D_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    alpha_P := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.P, alpha_P_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    alpha_C := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.C, alpha_C_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    comm := fun _ _ => rfl, cipher_z := fun _ => rfl, cipher_zeta := fun _ => rfl
  }
  comp f g := {
    alpha_D := g.alpha_D.comp f.alpha_D
    alpha_D_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_D g.alpha_D f.alpha_D_contractive g.alpha_D_contractive
    alpha_P := g.alpha_P.comp f.alpha_P
    alpha_P_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_P g.alpha_P f.alpha_P_contractive g.alpha_P_contractive
    alpha_C := g.alpha_C.comp f.alpha_C
    alpha_C_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_C g.alpha_C f.alpha_C_contractive g.alpha_C_contractive
    comm := fun d p => by dsimp; rw [f.comm d p, g.comm (f.alpha_D d) (f.alpha_P p)]
    cipher_z := fun p => by dsimp; rw [f.cipher_z, g.cipher_z]
    cipher_zeta := fun d => by dsimp; rw [f.cipher_zeta, g.cipher_zeta]
  }
/-- Multi-Modal Cognitive Agent Structure. -/
structure CognitiveAgent where
  Carrier : ContextObject
  AccessConsciousness : Prop
  InteractionCurvature : ℝ
  CechDescentDefect : ℝ
  access_requires_cross_coupling :
    AccessConsciousness → InteractionCurvature > 0
  coupling_forces_descent :
    InteractionCurvature > 0 → CechDescentDefect = 0
  access_requires_global_section :
    AccessConsciousness → CechDescentDefect = 0

def PhilosophicalZombie (N : CognitiveAgent) : Prop :=
  N.AccessConsciousness ∧ N.InteractionCurvature = 0

/-- Theorem: Impossibility of Philosophical Zombies. -/
theorem zombie_impossibility (N : CognitiveAgent) :
    PhilosophicalZombie N → False := by
  intro ⟨hAccess, hZeroCurv⟩
  have hCurvPos := N.access_requires_cross_coupling hAccess
  linarith

end Syntrometrie.CognitiveArchitecture

Appendix A (§A.3): Syntactic Cut Elimination (Gentzen’s Hauptsatz)

APPENDIX A (§A.3): DERIVATION HEIGHT (DEF. A.3), PERMUTATION (LEM. A.4), PRINCIPAL REDUCTION (LEM. A.5) & HAUPTSATZ (THM. A.6)

Derivation Height \(|\mathcal{D}|\) (Def. A.3) & Cut Permutation Lemma (Lem. A.4): * Height \(|\mathcal{D}|\): \(0\) on axioms \((\text{Ax}), (\text{Fact-S}_A), (\bot L)\); \(|\mathcal{D}_1|+1\) on unary rules; \(\max(|\mathcal{D}_1|,|\mathcal{D}_2|)+1\) on binary rules. * Lemma A.4 (Cut Permutation): If cut formula \(\psi\) is not principal in the final rule of \(\mathcal{D}_1\) or \(\mathcal{D}_2\), the Cut permutes upward to sub-derivations with strictly smaller height sum \(|\mathcal{D}_1'|+|\mathcal{D}_2'| < |\mathcal{D}_1|+|\mathcal{D}_2|\): - Case 1 (Left rules on \(\Delta\)): Permute Cut above \((\wedge L, \vee L, \to L)\) on auxiliary \(\chi \in \Delta\); height drops to \(|\mathcal{D}_{2a}| = |\mathcal{D}_2|-1\). - Case 2 (Right rules on \(\phi\)): Permute Cut across premises \(\mathcal{D}_{2a}, \mathcal{D}_{2b}\) of \((\wedge R)\). - Case 3 (Dynamic shift \([\pi_F]\text{-Step}\)): Preserves structure since \(\operatorname{Ext}_{[\pi_F]}(\Gamma,\Delta) = \operatorname{Ext}_{[\pi_F]}(\Gamma)\cup\operatorname{Ext}_{[\pi_F]}(\Delta)\).

Lemma A.5 (Principal Reduction) & Theorem A.6 (Gentzen’s Hauptsatz): If \(\psi\) is principal in both \(\mathcal{D}_1\) and \(\mathcal{D}_2\), the Cut on \(\psi\) reduces to Cuts on strictly lower-rank \(\psi'\) (\(\rk(\psi') < \rk(\psi)\)): 1. Conjunction (\(\psi_1\wedge\psi_2\), Fig. 45): Replace \((\wedge R)+(\wedge L)\) cut with sequential cuts on \(\psi_1\) and \(\psi_2\) plus Contraction \((\text{C})\). 2. Implication (\(\psi_1\to\psi_2\)): Cut \(\mathcal{D}_{2a}\vdash\psi_1\) with \(\mathcal{D}_{1a}:\Gamma,\psi_1\vdash\psi_2\), then cut \(\psi_2\) with \(\mathcal{D}_{2b}:\Delta',\psi_2\vdash\phi\). 3. Disjunction (\(\psi_1\vee\psi_2\)): Select matching premise \(\mathcal{D}_{2i}:\Delta,\psi_i\vdash^k\phi\) for \((\vee R_i)\) premise \(\Gamma\vdash^k\psi_i\). 4. Modal Necessity (\(\BoxS\theta\)): Apply \((\BoxS\text{-Ref})\) iteratively to \(\Gamma_0\) in \(\mathcal{D}_{1a}:\Gamma_0\vdash^k\theta\) to get \(\mathcal{D}_{1a}':\BoxS\Gamma_0\vdash^k\theta\), then cut directly on \(\theta\) with \(\mathcal{D}_{2a}:\Delta,\theta\vdash^k\phi\) (\(\rk(\theta) < \rk(\BoxS\theta)\)). 5. Dynamic Modality (\([\pi_F]\theta\)): Cut at level \(k+1\) on \(\theta\) between \(\mathcal{D}_{1a}\) and \(\mathcal{D}_{2a}\), then apply \(([\pi_F]\text{-Unstep})\). * Theorem A.6 (Cut Elimination): By double induction on \((\rk(\psi), |\mathcal{D}_1|+|\mathcal{D}_2|) \in \mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}_0\), every derivable sequent \(S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi\) has a pure cut-free derivation \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{norm}}\). \(\blacksquare\)
